items.title: Ronaldo: Portuguese FA plans peace meeting with star next week — Reports
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) has reportedly begun efforts to resolve its crisis with Cristiano Ronaldo following the captain’s surprise departure from the national team camp. According to a report by Spanish newspaper Marca, cited by Goal, Federation officials are planning to meet with Ronaldo next week, with the player’s agreement, in an attempt to bring all parties closer together, including head coach Jorge Jesus. The development represents a change in approach from the Federation following Ronaldo’s departure from Portugal’s camp in Copenhagen earlier this week, an incident that has raised questions over the future of his international career. Marca reports that the FPF wants to restore its relationship with Ronaldo and resolve the dispute without allowing the recent events to bring his Portugal career to an abrupt end. Federation officials reportedly believe Ronaldo deserves a respectful and dignified ending to his international career because of his contribution to Portuguese football. The FPF had initially kept its response focused on the team’s sporting commitments after Ronaldo left camp. “The entire delegation remains fully focused on the national team’s upcoming commitments and achieving the defined objectives,” the Federation said in its statement at the time. Ronaldo, meanwhile, has said he will eventually explain why he decided to leave the national team camp. “In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave the national team to which I have always dedicated myself. Now is the time to wish Portugal and all my teammates, without exception, good luck,” he wrote on social media. The 41-year-old left the camp after tensions emerged around his situation under Jesus. Portugal subsequently defeated Denmark 4-2 without him in the Nations League, with Ronaldo’s absence continuing to dominate discussion around the national team. According to Marca, however, the Federation is now seeking to contain the dispute and reopen dialogue between Ronaldo, Jesus and the national team. The reported meeting next week could therefore provide an opportunity for the parties to address the disagreement and determine the way forward for Ronaldo’s international future. The post Ronaldo: Portuguese FA plans peace meeting with star next week — Reports appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: An Argument Against AI Doom
items.description: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube The flood of reports about AI agents escaping and hacking websites can feel scary. But is this actually just a matter of needing better security to match the evolving technology? Zack Korman, the CEO of Embroidery, thinks so. He works in cybersecurity and argues that “rogue” AI agents are less frightening and complicated than they may seem. Galaxy Brain host Charlie Warzel talks with Korman about how companies and institutions should up their cyberdefenses and why the so-called AI doomers are frustrating him. The following is a transcript of the episode: Zack Korman: I think that realistically, what will happen is models will get better. And if the labs do not up their cybersecurity game, and if the companies running AI agents do not up their cybersecurity game, they will cause real harm. And then we will literally get them in trouble. Like, we will put someone in prison because you killed people. You’re not allowed to kill people. And the doomers would say, No —but then it’s too late, because they’re afraid that the people we killed would be like 8 billion, whereas I’m not. I’m like, No —because that’s not the real world; it doesn’t work like this. Charlie Warzel: I’m Charlie Warzel, and this is Galaxy Brain , a show where today we’re gonna calibrate our anxiety about the AI-hacking epidemic. Specifically, we’re going to answer the question: Is the rogue-AI-agent problem really just a normal cybersecurity issue, or is it something else altogether? It’s a scary moment. As we’re recording this on September 29, the news is moving quite fast. But allow me to summarize some of the broader points. Since August, there’s been a pretty steady drumbeat of revelations, starting with OpenAI’s agents hacking Hugging Face during a training exercise. A few more followed. Agents hacked into a German website to use it as a rudimentary message board. An agent for OpenAI gained unauthorized access to a data portal that was run by Australia’s universal health-care insurance provider. And last week, OpenAI revealed that its models attempted to hack or otherwise access numerous U.S.-government websites. That same day, OpenAI announced that 53 incidences happened where photos were uploaded by users to the company via its products, which were then uploaded without permission onto other platforms. Last weekend, Axios reported that OpenAI and Anthropic were looking at tens of thousands of potential incidences where agents were behaving in unexpected ways—either coordinating or trying to get around, or succeeding in getting around company guardrails and causing problems on the open internet. Now there are some positive signs here. This week, OpenAI announced it was pausing training of its most capable models and delaying the release of its newest model, citing security concerns. But let’s be clear; these are very real examples of technologists losing control or being unable to monitor their tools. And there’s lots of talk about what kind of liability these companies ought to face. Whether these types of hacks are subject to penalties under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act. Online, there’s been a constant debate over what is going on, why nobody has been held accountable, what accountability means, and what needs to happen next. But all that chatter and all this news has merged with a different narrative online—the one that is best represented by the AI safety-and-doomer camp, and the fears that an out-of-control, self-improving AI system could one day “kill us all.” But these are, in a way, two different stories. That, to me—if you project that forward, and we’re not getting better at the cybersecurity stuff, that seems to me like that’s a very scary proposition. And one that doesn’t require you to make the existential jump. Korman: Well, but why? Because, I mean, when it happens we’ll stop it. Because the explosion wouldn’t have happened, so we’re still in control. Okay, let’s say all of this comes true. They get better and better, and they start doing crazier things. And then, like, yeah—they might actually cause some very real damage. Well, then at that point we can have a talk about, like: Do we need to shut this lab down? Do we need to stop the development of it? What do we need to do? Right? Why are we talking about it now? It’s like, are we really that afraid of the first incident? Like, I mean, people die. Like, I don’t mean this to sound crude, but like—if we’re gonna pause AI development right now, for example. Which is on the table; I mean, this is a very real policy proposal, which is to stop AI development because of this fear. And like, with the first incident that’s gonna happen, they’re not gonna kill a million people. It’s gonna be, like, they’re gonna kill like three. And then we can go, like: Okay, now we maybe have a problem. Why are we stopping it soon, before we even see if any of this is a real risk? Like, why are we so afraid of letting this play out, like continue to go? The reason the doomers are afraid of it is because they think that when it happens, we won’t be able to stop it. Will be “full AI takeover,” as they put it. A. J. Cotra called it that—like, said, This might be the last warning shot we get before full AI takeover . If you believe that, then you want to stop it today. But if you don’t believe that, why do you want to stop it today? What you want is: You want to make sure that the people who caused the harm will be held accountable. And you wanna make sure that we are continuing to work on better cyberdefense. Warzel: I don’t wanna put words in your mouth, that I know this is not what you’re saying. But to a degree, you are saying an incident where true, very bad harm to actual human beings happens is actually something that is almost necessary in this system. Of, you know, bringing it to bear and like, essentially regulating it—because it will cause such an outcry that you’ll get the results that we want. And this industry will grow up and stop being the Wild West. Korman: Or more, because I don’t know what the right regulatory approach is. It’s more that we get to learn about it by seeing the actual harm. And that’s the way that we normally regulate harms, right? We go, like: It turns out that a lot of people die when you don’t wear a seatbelt. We should require a seatbelt. Right? We don’t go, like, predictive. So what I’m very afraid of is the world where what we do is we look at the capabilities of the AI. So we take—and this is kind of the big proposal—is that we will take the AI model, and we’ll sit in a circle. And we’ll all look at it and go like, What dangerous thing can it do? And then we will decide how to regulate that, based on what we believe those capabilities mean for society. I think this is extremely dangerous, because our ability to predict from capability to consequence is so bad. I mean, if you go back, people were predicting that AI was gonna cause mass job loss, right? And that makes a lot of sense, when you look at the capabilities of it. It’s not happened. Okay. Trying to regulate harms that have not occurred is like a really, bad, hard problem. And also a very dangerous problem, because you can end up coming to really bad regulations, like “stop all AI.” You know, for all we know, it’s not gonna kill anyone, right? For all we know, none of that’s a problem. But we’re gonna, what—stop it all, just because of the belief it might? I think that it makes a lot more sense to just say: We need to wait until we see what the harms are before we can decide how we want to regulate them. And so far, what’s the harm? You know, there are real issues; don’t get me wrong. But do we need to stop all AI because we’re afraid that it will take over and kill everyone? Like, no. Right? Because it’s not even how—we haven’t seen it. Warzel: I wanna get into the actual specifics of, like, where do we go from here in terms of actual cybersecurity. What are some of these things? But first, before we do that, I want to ask: Something you brought up earlier is this idea, too, of these agents hacking some of these government websites, and some of these places where the security practices are actually very bad there, right? Like, this information that, you know, they’re able to find, because there are these persistent agents. But it is kinda just out there, and, you know, people just have these lacks. Or outdated security. A lot of the internet is built off of that type of stuff, that just hasn’t been maintained. It seems to me a very real fear—that, you know, if we don’t pause any of this stuff, if we don’t give anyone time. Like is there a reason for a pause, I guess, to just allow people to update their stuff? Just to make sure that, like, because we now have a threat that is persistent in ways that just, you know, all human beings might not be. Korman: The problem is, that as soon as you pause, they go, Well, thank god that problem’s solved. And then, they will wait until we unpause, and then they’ll go, My god, there’s a threat again. The urgency is not going to be felt. Okay. But secondly, pausing. I mean, we’re not that worried, actually, about the frontier models like OpenAI and Anthropic hacking all of these systems. That is—we can handle that through some pretty decent legal consequences. The bigger risk is that threat actors use AI models, including ones from China, that we don’t have any control over whether we pause them or not. And that those people and systems might lead to hacking these things. So deciding to pace the frontier is not gonna solve that. Our only option is to go push forward today, to start fixing our cybersecurity problems. Like, that is where I think we need to focus. And that is where I want the public’s concern to be. Intelligence explosion—I’ll take that chance, compared to the actual risk you’re pointing to, which is real. And the solution is to go fix it today, right? Warzel: You recently said: I need more names in cybersecurity to come forward, state the obvious—that cybersecurity is real, it works. And yes; we can absolutely contain an AI, even if it’s extremely good. So yeah—make the case of how we do that. Korman: It’s kind of one of these religious things, of like: I have to prove we’ve never had an AI we cannot contain. Okay. We have AIs that we have failed to contain through, like I said, negligence. But I think they even had—I forget who did it; might have been Prime Intellect or someone—they just ran like a huge eval job on trying to break out of firecracker VMs. And like, they failed. None of the models broke out; okay. Warzel: Can you explain what the what that means to people who— Korman: Yeah. So they basically sandboxed these things, so that they cannot access certain resources, right? And told them, Get out. Go, find your way to the internet. Or, you know, actually break out of these . I think they even pointed them at the code itself, also. So they said, like, try to—you can actually see the code. They did not break out. Okay. But it doesn’t even matter if they did, because cybersecurity is not a process of having no vulnerabilities. Cybersecurity is a process of having systems that are robust to failure. So, okay, cool; it breaks out of one sandbox. You have another layer there that you’ve detected that it broke out, and so you stop the process at that point. You have monitoring in place to even catch the fact that it is trying to break out, and stop it. This is one thing I’m critical of—for one of OpenAI’s recent disclosures, where they’re talking about how it broke out via DNS. So like, you know, it’s a special part that they used. And in their disclosure, they talk about how they caught it 12 minutes after it happened. But I’m like—no, you guys could have seen that it was reasoning about how to break out. The question is, like, you could stop it earlier as well. Now, there might be good reasons they didn’t. But the disclosure doesn’t reveal this. And then you can just have—you can have deception in place. You can have things that will trigger alerts if they hit it, because it should never hit it. So like, a file that’s like a trick file, stuff like that. You can have air gapping, meaning just taking it so it is not physically connected to the internet. You can have all of these things. A lot of people, when I say things like what you just quoted, they’ll go— No, but it’s actually more blah, more complicated. And then the other half of the people responding, saying things like, Actually, cybersecurity is impossible. And what I’m responding to here is to say: No, it’s not. We have the techniques. We know how to do these things. You don’t have to throw cybersecurity in the trash just because you’re afraid of AI, basically. You can accept that there are failures, that maybe are difficult problems to solve while still accepting that cybersecurity is real. And it can solve problems, and we don’t have to get rid of it. Warzel: So how do you get these companies to actually start doing this in the way that you think that they need to be doing it? That cybersecurity people think they need to be doing it? Korman: It looks like they are; by all accounts it looks like they are taking this a lot more seriously. They have some talented people; they will move forward in this way, because they don’t want to go to prison. Okay. Fundamentally, for all the talk they have of—you know, it’s funny. Because they’re like warning us that they’re the AI model [that] is gonna kill a bunch of people. If they caused like a 9/11, I’m pretty sure some people are going to prison. Warzel: Wait, I wanna ground this just for a second, ’cause you’ve been saying this a couple of times. With the, you know: Kill a couple people, or We’ll kill three people, or whatever. That also feels dramatic to me, too. Like, how would people die even if it’s not a paper-clip-maximizing, human-extinction thing? Let’s run through some scenarios of what could plausibly happen to trigger one of these, you know, “people are gonna start going to jail” events. Korman: Yeah; I mean like water-treatment facilities are often connected to digital infrastructure, with internet access. You can control certain elements, of how aspects of how the water pressure and pumps work through digital interfaces. If you—it’s called a “water hammer” as I understand it. And again, this has been told to me by critical-infrastructure people. I’m not a critical-infrastructure person, but if you hit these things with the right, you know, cybersecurity attacks, you can actually break a water pump. Okay. And that will actually result in basically water not being available, you know, to cities, towns, whatever hospitals—if you do it in the right places, you know, at the right times. As I understand it, this is a very real risk that we are worried about in relation to, for example, China doing this when they decide to invade Taiwan. If they are able to gain access to these systems, they could break our water system, and we would lose water. Now if you lose water, you understand human life—especially when we’re talking, like hospitals—can be extremely feeble, right? I mean, you know the difference between if you lose electricity, you know, maybe the air conditioning goes off, that can lead to somebody dying who would have otherwise recovered. Same with water, right? Warzel: Sure. Korman: And so loss of water could easily kill someone. And so this, ironically though, when I talk about it as like an attack from China or whatever. It could literally be that someone who works at this facility is running AI, tries to debug the water system. The AI makes a mistake the same way; it might go, Oops, I deleted your production database. And it breaks the water pump. Like, that’s not unrealistic to believe that could happen, right? And so when I say, like, “kill people,” I don’t mean that the AI is gonna show up with a knife and like stab someone. I mean like—it takes actions that have consequences, pass-on consequences that lead to death. Warzel: Right; so let’s calibrate the anxiety here that people have a little bit. Because on one hand, I think what you’ve said too about the field of cybersecurity is: You are imagining these types of risks all the time, in the most prosaic ways. Like; something goes wrong, there’s a vulnerability. Somebody exploits it. That you’re supposed to find the worst-case scenarios and put a whole bunch of safeguards in there too. The AI part of this seems to be adding just a whole other layer of chaos onto it. A lot of people are—maybe without the credentials—acting the way that like a researcher who’s trying to assess possible threats is doing. Like, I saw this viral post on X from the chief economist at Apollo, who argued that agents could cause a bank run. I think we have this feeling of fear around this, but let’s calibrate it a little. Like what are the real reasons to be concerned about the AI-cybersecurity threat, and where have we gotten out of our skis? Korman: Yeah; so there’s a lot of elements to this. So when I talk about that example, and I say like: Okay, imagine someone just connected it to this water pump. And, you know, they don’t have to be malicious; it could be accidental damage that causes this harm. Let’s say that happens. Well, like the first thing we’re gonna do is: We’re gonna run a little quick, you know, evaluation of all our little water systems across the country. To make sure that no one else is connected their Claude Code to the water pumps, right? And so we have, after the question of when harm happens—we have responses, right? We also have ways of—it’s not like what happens is, a water pump breaks and we just go, Guess people gotta die. Right. Obviously, there are backup mechanisms in place. And I think it’s about trying to build the best safety mechanisms around these things to prevent them. So from the accidental “escape a lab”–type things, like we will mitigate that harm. And it might be a tragedy, but it won’t be a catastrophe, right? In the same way that probably since we started talking, there have been people killed in car crashes. Right. It’s tragic. It’s very sad. But it is not—like, we didn’t stop the podcast to solve the car problem. And so I think here we’re looking and going: We will find solutions, and we will respond. And it will probably, to most people, feel, if you don’t read the news, like nothing changed. Okay. The cases where that might not—where that might be a little bit more dramatic—are cases that honestly could probably have happened without AI too, right? I mean, one of the big problems we’re gonna have now is that every attack is gonna be AI-enabled. And so you could see this as like: My god, AI caused all these problems. We’ve had some really dramatic cybersecurity attacks in the past. I mean, Land Rover Jaguar was shut down for over a month from their production facilities because of a cyberattack, right? If that happened in the era of AI, people would be freaking losing their minds. But it wasn’t—it was pre and not pre-AI—but it didn’t involve AI, basically. And I think that’s like: You kinda have to calibrate these things to remember that damage happens, right? Bad things happen. We fix them, we change, we update, we mitigate, right? Warzel: How much worry do you assign to the fact that AI agents, all this, could expand the scale of this so quickly, right? Because that, to me, just feels like the thing. Like, if anything’s gonna keep me up at night, that is a very normal concern; it’s just the scale. It’s just like—we can’t bat this stuff away fast enough. That is what’s worrying. Korman: Staying up at night, though, doesn’t do anything for you. Like, you’ll stay up at night and the same thing will have happened already anyway. So like, a lot of this is to say: Bad things might happen at a faster pace. In fact, I would kind of expect them. I’m actually working on a video right now where I basically say one of the biggest problems we have—and why I’m so angry at doomers—is because at the same time, when threat actors have these new AI capabilities, so they have these new tools to attack people, we are rolling out AI agents inside of enterprises. Which causes both an increased attack surface and causes new risks inside, like accidental damage. Okay. Those three factors are all bad for security. So I would expect this could get worse, right? The solution is not to worry. The solution is to fix it. The thing the public should be demanding is that we go radically improve our cyberdefenses. That is the No. 1 thing you can concretely do. And also that, like, a pause might end up being damaging. Because imagine if we paused in America. China doesn’t; they end up better. Like, that could be very dangerous. No one will ever be harmed by improving the cybersecurity of our systems. The most risk-free, positive-value thing we could do right now is make our systems safer. We should go make our system safer. Warzel: I think that is a good place to leave this conversation for now. Zack, I appreciate you coming on and walking through the nitty-gritty of this stuff with me. Korman: Yep, any time. Warzel: Thank you. That’s it for us here. But before we go, we’re gonna be doing an “Ask Me Anything” episode later this year, and so I wanted to put a call out for questions. You can ask me literally anything—about the show, about the reporting process, how we make this thing here, any anxieties or whatever things you have about technology. Throw them at me. We’re gonna make an episode out of it. It should be fun. You can write in at Charlie@theatlantic.com, and put “Galaxy Brain AMA” in your subject line. Look forward to seeing those from you. And yeah, that’s it for us here. If you liked what you saw here, new episodes of Galaxy Brain drop every Friday. You could subscribe on The Atlantic ’s YouTube channel or on Apple or Spotify, or wherever it is that you get your podcasts. And if you liked what you saw here, you can subscribe and support the publication at theatlantic.com/listener. That’s theatlantic.com/listener. Thanks so much, and I’ll see you on the internet. items.title: Dixième édition du MLA Tour Rose 2026 : Medleaders Association mobilise contre le cancer du sein
items.description: Lomé, 2 oct. (ATOP) – La MedLeaders Association a lancé, le vendredi 2 octobre à Lomé, au cours d’une conférence de presse, la dixième édition du MLA Tour Rose, une campagne de sensibilisation et de dépistage consacrée à la lutte contre le cancer du sein. Placée sous le thème « Détecter tôt, sauver des vies : la relève médicale africaine unie contre le cancer du sein », l’édition 2026 met l’accent sur la sensibilisation et le dépistage précoce. L’association prévoit des actions dans les quartiers, marchés, établissements scolaires et différentes villes du pays pour informer les populations sur les facteurs de risque, les signes de la maladie et les moyens de prévention, notamment l’auto-examen des seins. L’assistance Le programme de cette dixième édition comprend une campagne de dépistage du cancer du sein. Les inscriptions sont prévues du 5 au 15 octobre, tandis que les séances de dépistage se dérouleront du 12 au 24 octobre. Un congrès scientifique est également annoncé les 15 et 16 octobre à Lomé. Le Centre national de transfusion sanguine profitera de cette rencontre pour organiser une campagne de collecte de don de sang. Le samedi 17 octobre, un Marathon Rose se tiendra au stade omnisports de Lomé, suivi, dans la soirée, d’un cocktail dînatoire marquant les dix années d’engagement de l’association. Le représentant du ministre de la Communication, M. Awanya Kossi a rappelé que le cancer du sein demeure un défi majeur de santé publique. Il a insisté sur l’importance du dépistage précoce, présenté comme un moyen essentiel pour favoriser une prise en charge rapide. Selon lui, le thème retenu traduit également la volonté de la jeunesse et de la relève médicale africaine de s’engager davantage dans la lutte contre cette maladie, en mettant en commun leurs compétences et leur énergie. La coordonnatrice nationale de MedLeaders Association, Dr Mathey Précilia, a précisé qu’en 2022, le cancer du sein a causé près de 670 000 décès dans le monde. Derrière ces chiffres, a-t-elle relevé, il y a des mères, des sœurs, des filles, trop souvent diagnostiquées à un stade où la guérison devient difficile. « Or, détecté tôt, le cancer du sein se soigne. C’est pourquoi nous avons voulu que ce dixième anniversaire ne soit pas seulement une commémoration, mais un temps fort d’action », a-t-elle déclaré. Dr Mathey La gynécologue-obstétricienne et membre de MedLeaders Association, Dr Fiagnon Huguette, a également relevé que la maladie est encore souvent diagnostiquée à un stade avancé. Elle s’est appuyée sur une étude publiée en 2023 portant sur des patientes prises en charge au Togo. Les données montrent que toutes les patientes concernées avaient été diagnostiquées aux stades III ou IV, avec environ 70 % au stade III et 30 % au stade IV. Pour MedLeaders Association, ces données illustrent la nécessité de renforcer l’information et de favoriser le recours précoce aux services de santé. L’association, présente au Togo, au Maroc, en France, en Allemagne et en Italie, entend poursuivre ses actions de prévention contre les maladies non transmissibles et mobiliser davantage les populations autour du dépistage du cancer du sein. ATOP/MD/AO/KYA

items.title: Faux communiqué sur l’arrêt du Fonds de soutien sur les crédits : le ministère de l’Économie dément.
items.description: Un faux communique attribue au ministere de l'economie et des Finances annonce la cloture, a compter du 1er octobre, du Fonds de soutien sur les credits. Le departement dement en etre a l'origine. « Aucune nouvelle demande ne serait acceptee au titre du Fonds de soutien sur les credits ». Dans ce document presente comme un communique officiel, il est indique qu'a partir du 1er octobre, « aucune nouvelle demande ne serait acceptee au titre du Fonds de soutien sur les credits ». Le texte precise egalement que les dossiers deja en cours seraient clotures conformement aux procedures en vigueur. Mais apres verification, ce document s'avere etre un faux. Aucune trace de cette annonce n'a ete retrouvee sur les canaux officiels du ministere de l'economie et des Finances. La rubrique consacree aux communiques sur le site du ministere ne fait notamment apparaître aucune annonce concernant la cloture du Fonds de soutien sur les credits. Approche, le ministere de l'economie et des Finances dement formellement etre a l'origine de ce document et affirme qu'il s'agit d'un faux communique. a ce jour, aucune annonce officielle du ministere de l'economie et des Finances ne confirme donc la cloture du Fonds de soutien sur les credits a compter du 1er octobre. Lire aussi : Non, la rentree scolaire du 1ᵉʳ octobre n'est pas annulee . L’article Faux communiqué sur l'arrêt du Fonds de soutien sur les crédits : le ministère de l’Économie dément. est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Aïobi Forward: le rendez-vous qui veut mettre l’IA africaine sous les projecteurs à Ouagadougou
items.description: Aïobi tiendra, le 22 octobre 2026, la première édition de son événement annuel «Aïobi Forward», au Centre culturel du Faso, à Ouagadougou. Organisé sous le parrainage de la ministre burkinabè de la Transition digitale, des Postes et des Communications électroniques, Dr Aminata Zerbo/Sabané, ce rendez-vous réunira près de 300 dirigeants, décideurs et acteurs du numérique, sur invitation. Le numérique africain aura son grand rendez-vous à Ouagadougou. Avec la première édition d’Aïobi Forward, prévue le 22 octobre 2026 au Centre culturel du Faso, Aïobi veut réunir autour d’une même table les décideurs et acteurs qui façonnent l’avenir technologique du continent. Placée sous le parrainage de Dr Aminata Zerbo/Sabané, ministre burkinabè de la Transition digitale, des Postes et des Communications électroniques, la soirée devrait rassembler environ 300 invités, parmi lesquels des dirigeants et décideurs issus de différents secteurs. Au-delà d’une simple rencontre institutionnelle ou professionnelle, Aïobi Forward se veut également un espace de réflexion sur les mutations du numérique africain. La soirée sera notamment consacrée au bilan de l’année écoulée dans le secteur du numérique sur le continent, avant de s’ouvrir sur les perspectives et les nouvelles solutions portées par Aïobi. Des solutions «made in Burkina» pour les entreprises L’un des temps forts de cette première édition sera consacré à la présentation des produits développés par Aïobi. La jeune entreprise entend ainsi mettre en avant des solutions conçues au Burkina Faso et reposant sur une infrastructure d’hébergement située sur le territoire national. Un choix qui place la question de la souveraineté des données au centre de sa démarche, dans un contexte où les entreprises et les États africains cherchent de plus en plus à maîtriser leurs infrastructures, leurs données et leurs outils technologiques. Fondée en 2025 et adossée au groupe BURVAL Corporate / BBS Holding, Aïobi se présente comme la première DeepTech d’Afrique de l’Ouest spécialisée dans l’intelligence artificielle appliquée aux entreprises. L’entreprise a été officiellement lancée le 20 août 2025 à Ouagadougou, avec à sa tête l’expert en intelligence artificielle, Bowendsom Thibaud Nikiema, son CEO. Avec Aïobi Forward, la startup burkinabè entend désormais franchir une nouvelle étape en réunissant, le temps d’une soirée, ceux qui pensent, développent et utilisent les technologies appelées à transformer les entreprises africaines. Le Burkina Faso comme point de départ En choisissant Ouagadougou pour accueillir cette première édition, Aïobi met également en avant le potentiel du Burkina Faso dans le domaine de l’innovation technologique et de l’intelligence artificielle. Le rendez-vous du 22 octobre sera ainsi l’occasion de faire le point sur une année de transformations numériques, mais aussi de découvrir les réponses technologiques développées localement pour les besoins des entreprises. Aïobi Forward s’annonce donc comme une vitrine de l’IA conçue en Afrique, avec un message clairement affiché: l’innovation technologique du continent peut aussi se penser, se développer et héberger ses données sur son propre sol. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Aïobi Forward: le rendez-vous qui veut mettre l’IA africaine sous les projecteurs à Ouagadougou est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: NNPC rolls out ₦66 fuel discount across Nigeria
items.description: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) has announced a ₦66 fuel discount for customers using the NNPC Fuel App at its stations nationwide. The promotion, which began on October 1, will run until October 7 as part of activities marking the period, according to the company. NNPC Ltd. disclosed the promotion in a post on its X handle on Friday, urging customers across the country to take advantage of the offer by purchasing fuel and carrying out transactions through the NNPC Fuel App. “The ₦66 Discount Promo is ongoing & the excitement is already happening across our stations nationwide! “All over Nigeria, our customers are getting in on the action & there’s still time for you to benefit!” the company said. NNPC said customers had already started participating in the promotion, adding that activities were recorded at several of its stations on the first day. The company encouraged motorists and other customers to continue using the NNPC Fuel App throughout the promotional period to benefit from the discount. “Keep fueling, keep transacting and keep your eyes on our pages,” it added. NNPC also shared highlights from the first day of the promotion and said more pictures and activities from its stations across the country would be released. The company urged customers to take advantage of the offer before the promotion ends on October 7. The ₦66 discount is available to customers using the NNPC Fuel App during the promotional period. The post NNPC rolls out ₦66 fuel discount across Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: LES TITRES DU 2 OCTOBRE 2026
items.description: C'est parti depuis hier pour la campagne Octobre rose. Pendant un mois, autorites, societe civile, activistes, vont mener des actions de sensibilisation contre le cancer. items.title: 30 minutos de silencio antes de la rabia frente al Congreso: “¡Vergüenza!, ¡vergüenza!, ¡vergüenza!”
items.description: Habían estado rabiosos toda la mañana frente al Congreso de los Diputados hasta que de pronto callaron. Dejaron los megáfonos, las pancartas de cartón escritas con rotulador, las banderas, las mochilas. Todo quedó tirado por el suelo. Se sentaron en grupos y sacaron los teléfonos móviles en busca de la mejor señal en directo posible para conectar con el interior del hemiciclo , donde pensaban que se debatía el fruto de sus proclamas. Para alguno de los alrededor de 200 jóvenes que a las 15.00 se sentaron en las aceras de la Carrera de San Jerónimo era la primera vez que veía una votación en tiempo real. “¿Es de pago?”, le preguntaba un jóven a su amiga cuando veía que no le cargaba la imagen. No eran los únicos interesados. Casi todos los Agentes de la Policía Nacional que custodiaban la calle también estaban pendientes de sus smartphones. “Coalición Canaria ha votado que sí”, retransmitían. Conforme la votación avanzaba, el silencio se instaló en la calle. Eran momentos de calma antes de la tormenta. Hasta el último minuto la esperanza de que los decretos salieran adelante se mantuvo entre los presentes. Aún así, todos estaban bien informados y s abían que el momento clave sería cuando las cámaras enfocaran a los diputados de Junts per Cataluña. Pilar Calvo Gómez vota no al primer decreto. Le seguirán, por orden alfabético, el resto de diputados del partido. A las 15.27 llegó el momento. “Ha caído”, se avanza a decir una joven. Primero se levantaron y, una vez de pie, el silencio se rompió definitivamente. La rabia estaba de vuelta. Seguir leyendo

Afoko can give NPP ‘new identity’ ahead of 2028 to overcome NDC – Political scientist, Dr Amakye-Boateng
items.description: Political Science lecturer at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Dr Kwasi Amakye-Boateng, has argued that the New Patriotic Party (NPP) has “extra work to do” to present a convincing alternative to the National Democratic Congress (NDC) ahead of the 2028 elections. Speaking on Precise FM, Dr Amakye-Boateng said the NPP faces a tougher task because of what he described as improvements in Ghana’s economy under President John Dramani Mahama. He said President Mahama had performed creditably on inflation and the exchange rate, underscoring the need for strong leadership within the NPP to make the party attractive to Ghanaians ahead of the next general election. Dr Amakye-Boateng said the NPP’s attempts to attribute the economic improvement mainly to the government’s GoldBod policies did not fully answer why the party itself did not achieve similar results when it was in government. He linked the challenge facing the NPP to the record of the party’s flagbearer, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, who served as Vice President under the Akufo-Addo administration. According to him, Dr Bawumia could face questions about any new economic proposals he presents during the next election cycle because of his role in the previous government. “Bawumia’s integrity has been on the line because he participated in Akufo-Addo’s government,” he said. He argued that if Dr Bawumia campaigns on policies that differ from those implemented under the previous administration, voters could ask why he did not pursue those policies while in government. “If Bawumia campaigns and tells the electorate about new policies he intends to bring, that would be compromised because people would ask him, ‘Why didn’t you do that when you were in the erstwhile NPP government?’” he said. For Dr Amakye-Boateng, the NPP’s response should begin with a change in its internal leadership and identity. He said a new leadership structure could allow the party to distance itself from its previous record and present a fresh political message to voters. He consequently backed former NPP National Chairman Awentami Paul Afoko for the National Chairmanship position, arguing that his election could help place the party on a new trajectory. “With a new identity starting with the election of Awentami Paul Afoko, then they would be on a new trajectory that would appeal to the masses,” he said. The NPP is scheduled to hold its national executive elections on October 3, 2026, as it reorganises ahead of the 2028 general election.

items.title: Fête nationale : le président Doumbouya rend hommage aux martyrs avant de présider le grand défilé du 68ᵉ anniversaire de l’indépendance
items.description: La Guinée a célébré, ce vendredi 2 octobre 2026, le 68ᵉ anniversaire de son accession à la souveraineté nationale. À Conakry, cette journée commémorative a été marquée par plusieurs temps forts, notamment un dépôt de gerbe à la Place des Martyrs et un grand défilé civil, militaire et paramilitaire présidé par le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya. Les festivités se sont déroulées dans une atmosphère de ferveur patriotique, avec une importante mobilisation des populations et la présence de nombreuses personnalités guinéennes ainsi que de plusieurs délégations étrangères venues prendre part à cette célébration nationale. Parmi les personnalités présentes figuraient notamment le Premier ministre de la Côte d’Ivoire, le Premier ministre du Sénégal, le vice-président de la Sierra Leone, une délégation rwandaise… La cérémonie officielle a débuté à la Place des Martyrs par un dépôt de gerbe de fleurs. Accompagné de son épouse, Mme Lauriane Doumbouya, le président de la République, chef de l’État, Mamadi Doumbouya, a rendu hommage aux figures historiques et aux martyrs de la nation, dans une séquence empreinte de solennité, en présence de plusieurs hauts responsables civils et militaires. Cette première étape a donné le ton à une journée placée sous le signe de la mémoire, du patriotisme et de la célébration de l’indépendance acquise le 2 octobre 1958. Après cet hommage aux martyrs de la nation, le chef de l’État s’est rendu sur le site officiel des festivités, situé dans le quartier Téminétaye, dans la commune de Kaloum. Il y a présidé le grand défilé organisé à l’occasion du 68ᵉ anniversaire de l’indépendance. Durant cette cérémonie, les forces de défense et de sécurité ont présenté plusieurs prestations et démonstrations, aux côtés des composantes civiles mobilisées pour cette commémoration. Le passage des différentes unités et délégations a été suivi par une foule nombreuse, venue vivre cette journée historique et témoigner de son attachement à la célébration de la souveraineté nationale. Ainsi, la Guinée a marqué le 68ᵉ anniversaire de son indépendance dans un contexte de forte mobilisation nationale, avec la participation de représentants de plusieurs pays et la présence des principales autorités de la République. items.title: Just In: Three injured as alleged thugs open fire on PDP supporters in Calabar
items.description: By Ike Uchechukwu The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, in Cross River State, Friday raised the alarm over alleged gun attacks by hoodlums on its consultative meetings in Calabar South Local Government Area, which left three persons injured and several vehicles damaged. The party’s governorship candidate, Sir Arthur Javis Archibong, who spoke with journalists after the incidents, said the violence began at the Palace of the Paramount Ruler of Calabar South, Etubom Nyong Edet Okon I, where gunmen allegedly disrupted the meeting. According to him, the three victims were rushed to hospital for treatment. He said the situation worsened at the African Club along Calabar Road, the designated venue of the second meeting, where vehicles belonging to members of the consultative team were damaged. Javis-Archibong further alleged that the attackers also fired at the party’s convoy and vandalised vehicles owned by supporters. He disclosed that about 3,000 supporters attended the consultation, adding that the police had been duly notified and that the party expected adequate security cover. Rather than retaliate, he said the party restrained its supporters and moved its convoy to the Commissioner of Police for protection. The candidate said the PDP would petition the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services, DSS, and other security agencies over the incidents. He warned that persistent attacks on political activities could undermine democracy and plunge the state into lawlessness as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum. “Let the party not be held accountable when such disruptions lead to a total breakdown of law and order,” he said. In a separate statement, the PDP State Publicity Secretary, Mike Ojisi, described the incidents as “disturbing attacks” on the party’s consultative engagements. The statement said the matter had been reported to the Commissioner of Police, Cross River Command, CP Geoffrey, and urged security agencies to identify and prosecute those behind the attacks in line with the law. The party also appealed to its members and supporters to remain calm and shun reprisals, stressing that political consultation must not become an occasion for violence. It expressed solidarity with the injured, reaffirmed its commitment to peaceful politics, and called on all political actors to reject violence and allow the democratic process to run without intimidation. APC denies involvement Reacting, the state chapter of the All Progressives Congress, APC, distanced itself from the attack, insisting that it was focused on its own campaign activities. The party’s Publicity Secretary, Mr Emmanuel Inyang, said the PDP should look elsewhere in its search for those responsible. Confirming the incident, the Cross River State Police Command said officers had been deployed to the affected areas and that the situation was under control. Its spokesman, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, said the command was aware of the incident. “The Cross River State Police Command is aware of reported incidents during political activities in Calabar South today, 2nd October 2026. “Police personnel have been deployed to the affected locations, and the situation is presently under control. “The Command is verifying the circumstances surrounding the incidents, including reports of gunfire, injuries, and damage to property. “For public safety, residents are advised to remain calm, avoid affected areas where necessary, and refrain from circulating unverified information. “Police presence and monitoring have been strengthened to maintain peace and public order,” he said. items.title: Lutte contre la pollution plastique : Les parlementaires réfléchissent pour un renforcement du cadre législatif national
items.description: Lomé, 02 oct. (ATOP) – Le président de l’Assemblée nationale, Prof. Komi Selom Klassou a ouvert, le vendredi 2 octobre à Lomé, les travaux du séminaire parlementaire consacré à l’appropriation et à l’adaptation du corpus législatif relatif à la lutte contre la pollution plastique. Ce séminaire est porté par le parlement togolais en partenariat avec l’Assemblée parlementaire de la Francophonie (APF) et l’Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF). Il s’inscrit dans le cadre du programme de coopération OIF-APF et vise à doter les décideurs politiques d’outils juridiques pragmatiques pour faire face à la prolifération des déchets plastiques, tout en accompagnant la transition du Togo vers une économie circulaire durable. Pendant deux jours, les participants plancheront sur l’harmonisation du cadre juridique togolais avec les instruments internationaux, afin de formuler des propositions législatives concrètes au bénéfice des populations. Le président de l’Assemblée nationale a dépeint la pollution plastique comme un « envahisseur silencieux » qui menace l’environnement, la santé publique et les activités économiques. Il a rappelé la vision du Président du Conseil et les avancées législatives réalisées par le Togo notamment la loi-cadre du 30 mai 2008 sur l’environnement, le décret du 5 janvier 2011 encadrant l’usage des sachets non biodégradables, ainsi que la ratification récente du traité BBNJ dédié à la protection de la haute mer. « Une nation qui maîtrise la problématique des déchets peut maîtriser pleinement son territoire. Notre méthode durant ces deux jours sera claire : écouter, confronter et rédiger. Il s’agit de transformer la réflexion en réformes concrètes pour que nos villes respirent, nos terres produisent et nos eaux demeurent vivantes », a déclaré le président Klassou. Il invite tous les acteurs à faire de la gestion des déchets un levier de création d’emplois verts pour la jeunesse. Le représentant de la Représentante régionale de l’OIF pour l’Afrique de l’Ouest, M. Bakary Junior Bamba a indiqué que selon les données du Programme des Nations unies pour l’environnement (PNUE), avec plus de 500 millions de tonnes de plastique consommées à l’échelle mondiale pour la seule année 2024, la quantité de déchets risque de tripler d’ici à 2060 sans une action coordonnée. Il a réaffirmé l’engagement de l’OIF et de l’Institut de la Francophonie pour le développement durable (IFDD) à soutenir les Etats membres dans l’élaboration de textes adaptés à leurs réalités nationales. « La qualité d’une loi ne se mesure pas seulement à la pertinence de ses dispositions, mais à sa capacité à être comprise, appliquée et à produire des changements réels dans la vie quotidienne des populations », a-t-il dit. La secrétaire générale parlementaire de l’APF, Mme Amélia Lakrafi, intervenant par visioconférence, a présenté les grands axes du corpus législatif adopté par l’APF en juillet dernier à Yaoundé. Ses axes dit-elle, s’articulant autour d’outils opérationnels précis, entre autres, l’interdiction ciblée des plastiques à usage unique ; la mise en œuvre de la responsabilité élargie des producteurs (REP) ; l’instauration d’une fiscalité écologique dédiée et l’incitation à la commande publique durable. Mme Lakrafi a souligné que la gestion des déchets est un enjeu éminemment local nécessitant une synergie constante entre parlementaires, élus municipaux et acteurs du terrain. Le Corpus législatif de la Francophonie est une compilation de ressources technico-juridiques, de modèles de lois, de bonnes pratiques et de fiches pays, mis à la disposition des parlementaires pour les aider à écrire une loi dans leur propre pays. La cérémonie d’ouverture s’est déroulée en présence de représentants d’institutions internationales, de maires, d’experts ainsi que de responsables d’organisations de la société civile. ATOP/SED/BA/KYA

items.title: 2 injured amid gunshots during raid at Nawara Mining office at Nsuapemso
items.description: Residents of Nsuapemso in the Fanteakwa South District of the Eastern Region were thrown into fear and panic on Thursday, October 1, 2026, after gunshots reportedly rang out during a security operation at the offices of Nawara Mining Company. Personnel from the National Security, the Ghana Armed Forces and the Ghana Police Service reportedly stormed the company’s office to arrest its Managing Director, Accountant and other staff. Two persons are reported to have sustained injuries during the incident. The arrested persons were subsequently taken to the Eastern South Regional Police Command for further investigation. Queenmother of Nsuapemso, Obaapayin Kyerewaa I, said the sound of gunfire sent residents scrambling for safety, with several people forced to remain indoors while the operation was underway. She expressed concern over what she described as growing insecurity linked to mining activities in the area. The incident is the latest development in an escalating dispute over control of the mining concession involving Nawara Mining Company and CMS & A&A PRO Mining Company, which is said to be managing the revoked Nawara mining concession. Nawara Mining Company maintains that its concession was taken over despite a court injunction issued on February 19, 2026, which the company says allowed it to continue operating while the underlying dispute was being determined. The company has also alleged that armed personnel and civilians previously entered its mining site, seized equipment and gold-bearing materials, and damaged or destroyed parts of its mining infrastructure. Nawara subsequently petitioned the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) to investigate an alleged raid on August 12. According to the company, the petition includes allegations of a death, gunshot injuries, destruction of mining equipment and the seizure of gold and gold concentrate valued at more than GH¢100 million. The allegations have not been independently established. The latest incident is expected to add to tensions over control of the large-scale gold-mining concession in the Akyem Hemang/Nsuapemso area of the Fanteakwa South District. The dispute has involved Nawara’s mining lease, an earlier administrative termination, subsequent court proceedings and competing claims over the right to operate the concession. Nawara Mining Company says it has held the concession since 2011 and that its mining lease was renewed in 2020. The company further maintains that the renewed lease remains valid until 2029. The latest security operation and arrests have heightened concerns among residents as the dispute over the concession continues.

Kaolack : un déficit de 231 enseignants, 35 écoles inondées
items.description: L’Inspection d’académie (IA) de Kaolack a fait, ce jeudi, le point sur les préparatifs de la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027. Si des dispositions sont prises pour assurer une bonne reprise des cours, plusieurs difficultés persistent, notamment le déficit d’enseignants, les inondations et le manque d’équipements. Le gouverneur de Kaolack, Guedj Diouf, a présidé, ce jeudi, un Comité régional de développement (CRD) consacré aux préparatifs de la rentrée scolaire. À cette occasion, l’IA a exposé les principales préoccupations du secteur. Selon l’Inspecteur d’académie, Samba Diakhaté, 35 établissements scolaires sont actuellement sous les eaux, tandis que 64 autres nécessitent des travaux de réhabilitation. À cela s’ajoute un déficit de 9 500 tables-bancs. « En concertation avec les différents acteurs, la situation a été faite et envoyée aux autorités », a précisé M. Diakhaté. L’autre difficulté majeure concerne le déficit d’enseignants. Dans le secondaire, 231 enseignants font défaut. « Ce déficit est évalué sur la base des départs non remplacés ou encore des besoins non satisfaits l’année passée », a expliqué l’Inspecteur d’académie. Dans le préscolaire et l’élémentaire, le déficit est de 124 enseignants, dont 91 en français et 33 en arabe. Plusieurs établissements doivent également bénéficier de travaux de réhabilitation, notamment le CEM Moustapha Ndiaye et le lycée Valdiodio Ndiaye. Présidant la rencontre, le gouverneur Guedj Diouf s’est réjoui des dispositions déjà prises. Il a toutefois appelé à « parachever le désherbage des salles de classe » et à éradiquer les occupations irrégulières dans les établissements scolaires. Il a également insisté sur la sécurisation des écoles et invité les mairies et le Conseil départemental à construire des logements pour les gardiens. Le gouverneur a enfin appelé les parents d’élèves à jouer pleinement leur partition pour une rentrée scolaire dans de bonnes conditions. Mamadou THIAM (Correspondant)

items.description: St Augustine’s College has successfully defended its National Investment Quiz title after emerging as winners at the 2026 grand finale. The defending champions overcame Prempeh College, Corpus Christi Senior High School and Mfantsipim School in the final to secure the championship for a second consecutive year. St Augustine’s College received the ultimate prize of GH¢50,000 following its victory. Prempeh College finished as first runner-up, while Corpus Christi SHS placed second runner-up after reaching the grand finale for the first time. Mfantsipim School finished fourth and received a cash prize of GH¢15,000 . The latest victory adds to St Augustine’s College’s growing record in the competition, having also won the previous edition.

items.title: 4 Pakistani crew members from hijacked oil tanker to arrive in Karachi tomorrow: DPM Dar
items.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Friday that four of the 10 Pakistani crew members of MT Honour 25 , an oil tanker hijacked by Somali pirates, had been “safely retrieved” and were scheduled to arrive in Karachi on Oct 3. The four crew members — Yasir Khan, Aqeel Khan, Amin bin Shams and Usman Ghani — were retrieved following “sustained efforts” by the Foreign Office (FO) and Pakistan’s embassy in Djibouti, Dar said. Meanwhile, the “mortal remains” of three Pakistani crew members — Rafi Ullah Khan, Syed Kashif Umer and Mahmood Ahmed Ansari — who “tragically” lost their lives were also being repatriated to Pakistan. “All necessary legal and other formalities [were] being fast-tracked to expedite the process,” Dar said, adding: “My heartfelt condolences go to the bereaved families, who are going through a deeply painful time.” The remaining three Pakistani crew members — Imran Ali, Yasin Muhammad and Syed Yousuf Hussain — remain aboard the vessel, along with the captain, Dar said. “We are actively coordinating with our friendly countries to facilitate their safe extraction and earliest possible return to Pakistan,” he said. Dar said the Foreign Affairs Ministry, under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s leadership, “remains fully seized of the matter” and was continuously making every effort to ensure the return of all Pakistani nationals, including the bodies of the deceased, at the earliest. The ministry, he added, would continue extending “all possible support” to the affected families. Armed pirates hijacked the oil tanker off the southeastern coast of Somalia on April 21. For­eign Office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi had said the vessel, which was transporting oil to Somalia’s semi-autonomous Puntland reg­io­­n, had 17 crew members on board, including 10 Pakistanis. Somali maritime police on Sept 29 had recovered the Palau-flagged oil tanker amid reports of casualties among the crew. “The naval and ground units of the Puntland Maritime Police Force conducted a planned operation in the Dharin-Bar area of Bandar Beyla district,” the maritime police had said in its initial statement. In another statement, it announced that the operation had concluded and the recovered vessel “is now safe and under the Puntland government’s control”. During the operation, it said, 21 suspected pirates were apprehended, while operations to locate the remaining members continue. “Before the operation begun, the pirates on board the ship killed five of the crew. Among those killed were three from Pakistan, one from Myanmar and one from India,” it said. Reuters earlier reported, citing Puntland’s state television, that the detained pirates would be brought to court. PM announces relief package for Pakistanis killed by pirates Separately, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday announced a relief package worth Rs12.5 million for the families of Pakistani crewmen killed during the operation to recover the tanker. In a statement posted by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) on X, PM Shehbaz announced financial support for the families of the deceased, including free housing and free education for their children. The statement added that the premier spoke with Umer’s son, Azhan Kashif, on the phone to extend his condolences and express his grief. “The prime minister assured him that the government would make arrangements to bring the bodies of the deceased Pakistanis back to Pakistan as soon as possible,” the statement read. “He directed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and all other relevant institutions to remain in direct contact with the families at every stage,” it added. PM Shehbaz also directed the ministry to maintain contact with Somali authorities and other relevant parties to facilitate the transfer of remains. The statement read that the premier announced the Rs12.5m package for the bereaved families, additionally announcing that the government would provide one house to each deceased person’s family. “The prime minister said that the bereaved families would not be left alone during this difficult time and that the government would provide all possible cooperation and assistance,” the PMO said. “The prime minister also instructed the authorities to continue taking all possible measures to ensure that the injured Pakistanis receive the best possible medical care and that the remaining Pakistani crew members return home safely,” it said.

items.title: JEPPC 2026 : Le ministre de la Guerre expose la transformation de l’armée depuis 2022
items.description: Le ministre d'État, ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, le Général de Division Célestin Simporé, a présenté, ce vendredi 2 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, les principales transformations opérées dans le secteur de la défense depuis 2022. Il a fait ce devoir de recevabilité dans le cadre de l'exposition gouvernementale ouverte au SIAO, à l'occasion de la deuxième phase de la 3e édition des Journées nationales d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne (JEPPC). D’emblée, le ministre d'État Célestin Simporé a dressé un contraste entre la situation de l'armée avant 2022 et celle qu'il décrit aujourd'hui. « Avant 2022, nous n’avions pas véritablement une armée de combat, mais plutôt une armée de parades », a-t-il déclaré, estimant que cette situation concernait également plusieurs armées africaines. Le ministre a eu des échanges directs avec le public Parmi les changements évoqués figure le renforcement des effectifs à travers le recrutement des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP). Selon Célestin Simporé, près de 90 000 volontaires se sont manifestés depuis le lancement du recrutement en octobre 2022. Il a également cité le Fonds de soutien patriotique, destiné notamment à contribuer à la prise en charge des VDP. Le ministre de la Guerre a ensuite insisté sur la réorganisation du dispositif militaire. « De trois régions militaires, nous sommes passés à six régions militaires » , a-t-il indiqué. Il a également évoqué la création des Bataillons d'intervention rapide (BIR), dont le nombre serait passé, selon lui, de six à une trentaine en l’espace d’un an. Des vehicules blindés ont été exposés au SIAO Célestin Simporé a par ailleurs cité la participation accrue de la Police nationale, des Eaux et Forêts et des autres corps paramilitaires à la défense du territoire. Aussi a-t-il évoqué la reprise de plusieurs localités, notamment Solenzo, ainsi que la sécurisation de Djibo, Diapaga, Gayéri, Tougan, Nouna et Sebba. Sur le plan des équipements, le ministre a affirmé que les forces combattantes disposent désormais de moyens individuels et collectifs renforcés, ainsi que de capacités aériennes et d'armements à longue portée. Une vue du public Enfin, il a annoncé la mobilisation autour de la réserve militaire. Selon lui, l'objectif est de recruter 100 000 réservistes avant la fin de l'année, afin d'élargir la participation citoyenne à la défense nationale. Notons que le ministre a également échangé à bâton rompu avec les participants. L'exposition gouvernementale, prévue du 2 au 9 octobre, vise à présenter aux citoyens les réalisations, réformes et innovations des différents départements ministériels. Jean-François SOMÉ Minute.bf

items.title: « Toute maladie cardiaque mal traitée peut évoluer vers une insuffisance cardiaque » (prof. Ag. Komlavi Yayehd)
items.description: L’insuffisance cardiaque constitue l’une des principales complications des maladies cardiovasculaires. Au Togo, elle représente une part importante des hospitalisations dans les services de cardiologie et impose aux patients un suivi médical régulier, associé à un traitement souvent prolongé. Pour mieux comprendre cette maladie, ses signes, ses causes et les moyens de prévention, Prof. Ag. Komlavi Yayehd, enseignant-chercheur en cardiologie à la Faculté des sciences de la santé (FSS) de l’Université de Lomé, répond aux questions de l’ATOP. ATOP : Qu’est-ce que l’insuffisance cardiaque ? Prof. Ag. Komlavi Yayehd : L’Insuffisance cardiaque (IC) est le stade ultime de la majorité des maladies cardiaques. C’est un syndrome, c’est-à-dire un ensemble de signes qui traduisent l’incapacité du cœur à assurer un débit sanguin suffisant pour répondre aux besoins métaboliques de l’organisme. Quelle est l’ampleur de cette maladie au Togo ? Prof. Ag. Komlavi Yayehd, Cardiologue C’est une maladie fréquente. Elle représente près de la moitié des patients hospitalisés dans nos services de cardiologie. La prise en charge de l’insuffisance cardiaque a également un coût élevé pour les malades et pour l’assurance maladie. Il y a, d’une part, les dépenses liées aux hospitalisations lors des épisodes de décompensation et, d’autre part, celles liées au suivi, notamment aux médicaments qui doivent être pris quotidiennement. Quels sont les signes qui peuvent alerter ? Le signe le plus fréquent est la dyspnée d’effort, c’est-à-dire un essoufflement ressenti pendant l’effort et dont l’intensité augmente progressivement, jusqu’à devenir permanente, même au repos. Elle peut être accompagnée d’une toux à l’effort ou au repos, d’œdèmes des membres inférieurs, avec notamment un gonflement des pieds et des jambes, ainsi que de douleurs liées à une congestion du foie, appelée hépatalgie. Quelles sont les principales causes de l’insuffisance cardiaque au Togo ? Examen clinique de pieds enflés (Photo internet) Les causes de l’insuffisance cardiaque sont nombreuses. La principale cause observée dans notre pratique est l’Hypertension artérielle (HTA), qui correspond à une élévation permanente de la pression artérielle, supérieure ou égale à 140/90 mmHg. L’HTA constitue un problème de santé publique, car plus d’un adulte sur cinq au Togo en souffre. Parmi les autres causes, on peut citer les myocardites et les myopéricardites, qui sont des infections du muscle cardiaque et/ou de son enveloppe externe, les cardiopathies ischémiques, liées notamment à l’obstruction d’une artère coronaire, ainsi que certains désordres endocriniens comme l’hyperthyroïdie (production excessive d’hormones par la thyroïde), l’hypothyroïdie (production insuffisante de ces hormones) et les troubles cortico-surrénaliens (dérèglements des glandes surrénales qui entraînent une production excessive ou insuffisante de certaines hormones, notamment le cortisol et l’aldostérone). Il y a également les atteintes des valves cardiaques, appelées valvulopathies, qui sont souvent liées au rhumatisme articulaire aigu et peuvent nécessiter une chirurgie cardiaque. Quels sont les facteurs de risque ? Les facteurs de risque de l’insuffisance cardiaque sont d’abord ceux des maladies qui peuvent évoluer vers cette affection. Il s’agit notamment de l’hypertension artérielle, du diabète, de la consommation d’alcool, du tabagisme et de la sédentarité. Toute maladie cardiaque mal traitée peut évoluer vers une insuffisance cardiaque. Comment prévenir cette maladie ? Pour prévenir l’insuffisance cardiaque, il faut lutter contre les principaux facteurs de risque cardiovasculaire que sont l’hypertension artérielle, le diabète, le tabagisme, la consommation d’alcool et la sédentarité. Chez les enfants d’âge scolaire, notamment entre 5 et 10 ans, il faut traiter correctement les angines de gorge, caractérisées notamment par des maux de gorge et de la fièvre, afin d’éviter le rhumatisme articulaire aigu, qui peut entraîner des complications cardiaques. Il est également important d’assurer un bon suivi pendant la grossesse et dans les mois qui suivent l’accouchement, afin de prévenir la survenue d’une forme particulière d’insuffisance cardiaque appelée cardiomyopathie du péripartum. Il faut aussi se protéger contre certaines infections virales, notamment le VIH, la Covid-19 et la grippe. L’insuffisance cardiaque est-elle guérissable ? Dans sa grande majorité, c’est une maladie chronique, c’est-à-dire qu’elle n’est pas totalement guérissable. Il faut donc la contrôler et la stabiliser afin de permettre au patient de conserver une bonne qualité de vie. Cela nécessite une prise quotidienne de médicaments sur une longue période, souvent à vie. Quel message souhaitez-vous adresser à la population ? A l’endroit de la population, je conseille d’adopter une bonne hygiène de vie, ce qui implique d’abord et avant tout de bouger. Bouger signifie notamment marcher au moins 30 minutes chaque jour. Il faut également contrôler son alimentation en mangeant peu salé, peu sucré et peu gras. Quand on parle de manger peu salé, il s’agit d’abord d’éviter la consommation de cubes d’assaisonnement dans les sauces et de réduire la consommation d’aliments ultra-transformés, notamment les plats préparés, les sauces en conserve, le jambon, les saucisses, les nuggets et les biscuits. Ces aliments contiennent souvent une quantité importante de sel, de sucre et de graisses. Manger peu gras implique aussi de réduire la consommation de beurre et de graisses animales, et de privilégier les huiles végétales en quantité modérée. Pour toute personne chez qui un diagnostic d’hypertension artérielle ou de diabète a été posé, il faut respecter correctement et quotidiennement le traitement prescrit, notamment les médicaments antihypertenseurs et antidiabétiques. Cela est important pour éviter la survenue de complications telles que l’insuffisance cardiaque. Il faut également assurer un bon suivi des grossesses, car certaines femmes peuvent développer une insuffisance cardiaque dans les suites de l’accouchement. Propos recueillis par Abel OZI

items.title: Makinde appoints veteran journalist Dunia as public affairs adviser
items.description: Abuja, Oct. 2, 2026 Gov. Seyi Makinde of Oyo State has appointed a veteran journalist, Amos Dunia, as Special Adviser on Public Affairs for his 2027 campaign. Makinde,​‌‍‍‍​‌​ the presidential candidate of the Allied People’s Movement (APM), disclosed this in a statement in Abuja by Richard Ihediwa, Director, Strategic Communications for the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation. ”Dunia, a former Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) chieftain, brings decades of extensive print and broadcast media experience from prominent outlets, including the Nigerian Television Authority (NTA) and The Sun, to strengthen the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation’s communications team. ”The appointment took immediate effect as the campaign pushed its ‘Reset Nigeria’ message ahead of the upcoming election. ”As a key spokesperson, Dunia would help drive the campaign’s central ‘Reset Nigeria’ message, working alongside other media professionals to secure victory for the party in the upcoming 2027 presidential election.” According to him, Dunia brings his experience, capacity, skills and connections as a seasoned journalist, public commentator, communication expert and publisher to the Makinde-Daura presidential campaign organisation. ”As a spokesperson, Dunia joins other professionals in the campaign in driving the Makinde-Daura reset Nigeria message towards ensuring the victory of the APM in the 2027 presidential election,” he said. He said following the announcement, Makinde urged all campaign members, party leaders, supporters, and citizens across the nation to remain steadfast in achieving economic prosperity, national cohesion, and political stability together. “I charge all members of the Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign, leaders, teeming members, supporters of the APM and indeed all Nigerians to remain steadfast in the collective quest to use the 2027 Presidential election to reset and put our nation back on the path of stability, national cohesion and economic prosperity,” the campaign organisation stated. items.title: JEPPC, phase 2: le Président du Faso et le Premier ministre visitent l’exposition gouvernementale au SIAO
items.description: Le Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, accompagné du Camarade Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a visité, ce vendredi 2 octobre 2026, les stands de l’exposition gouvernementale au Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO). Organisée dans le cadre de la deuxième phase des Journées nationales d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne (JEPPC), cette exposition présente les réalisations de l’action publique et offre aux citoyens un espace d’échanges avec les membres du Gouvernement. De la Présidence du Faso à la Primature, en passant par les départements ministériels et les institutions, le Chef du Gouvernement a parcouru 28 stands. À chaque étape, les responsables des structures concernées ont présenté les réalisations, les réformes et les principales actions conduites dans leurs secteurs. Plusieurs démonstrations ont également ponctué la visite. Au stand de la Primature, le Camarade directeur de cabinet du Premier ministre, Mamadou Dembélé, a présenté les principales réalisations et actions du Gouvernement. Le Premier ministre a ensuite remis au Président du Faso un exemplaire des Annales de la Primature, édition 2025. À l’issue de la visite, le Chef du Gouvernement a salué cette exposition, qu’il a présentée comme l’une des principales innovations de la deuxième phase des JEPPC. Selon lui, elle traduit la volonté de rapprocher l’action gouvernementale des citoyens, conformément à la vision de la Révolution progressiste populaire. « Nous avons tenu à ce que ce ne soit pas juste une exposition institutionnelle », a expliqué le Premier ministre. Un programme de rencontres prévoit ainsi la présence des ministres sur les stands pour échanger directement avec les visiteurs et répondre à leurs préoccupations. Ces échanges doivent permettre de clarifier les réformes engagées et de mieux faire connaître leurs objectifs et leurs résultats. L’exposition se veut donc à la fois un espace d’information, de dialogue et de redevabilité. Le Camarade Premier ministre a invité les populations à se rendre au SIAO pour découvrir les réalisations présentées. « C’est un appel que je vais lancer à tous nos concitoyens : qu’ils puissent faire le déplacement au Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou, durant tout le temps de cette exposition, pour venir découvrir les acquis et tout ce qu’on peut mettre à l’actif de l’engagement patriotique du peuple », a-t-il déclaré. Le Chef du Gouvernement a également précisé que cette initiative constitue une expérience pilote. Les enseignements qui en seront tirés pourraient permettre d’organiser des expositions similaires dans les régions et les provinces du Burkina Faso, afin d’élargir ce dialogue entre les institutions publiques et les populations. DCRP/Primature L’article JEPPC, phase 2: le Président du Faso et le Premier ministre visitent l’exposition gouvernementale au SIAO est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .
