items.title: Kindia : la fête de l’indépendance célébrée sous le signe de la paix et de la solidarité
items.description: La République de Guinée a célébré, ce vendredi 2 octobre 2026, le 68ᵉ anniversaire de son accession à l’indépendance. À Kindia, située à 135 kilomètres de Conakry, la commémoration s’est déroulée sans défilé. Les autorités administratives, sécuritaires, éducatives et locales se sont retrouvées à la Place des Martyrs pour un dépôt de gerbes, avant de délivrer des messages axés sur la paix, l’unité nationale et la solidarité. La cérémonie a débuté par l’accueil des autorités par les populations de Kindia, venues nombreuses à la Place des Martyrs. Après le dépôt de gerbes, plusieurs responsables ont pris la parole pour rappeler l’importance de cette date historique et appeler à préserver la paix et la cohésion nationale. Prenant la parole, le maire de la commune urbaine de Kindia, Aboubacar Molota Camara, a déclaré : « Aujourd'hui, c'est un grand jour pour nous. Nous ne sommes pas historiens, mais nous savons que le 28 septembre 1958 a donné naissance au 2 octobre et c'est pour cette raison que nous sommes dans un élan de ferveur. On appelle le militantisme, nous avons notre liberté, notre indépendance. Et aujourd'hui, nous sommes à la conquête de notre indépendance économique. Cela s'est déjà fait sentir, parce que le programme de société de M. le Président de la République, qui est incarné à travers Simanou 2040, est l'expression la plus vivante que la Guinée, a bougé et la Guinée est en train de bouger. Merci encore une fois, M. le Président. » Pour sa part, le préfet de Kindia, le colonel Abdourahmane Keïta, a, dans son discours, rendu hommage aux acteurs de l’indépendance avant d’adresser un message particulier à la jeunesse guinéenne. « Ce jour solennel du 2 octobre 2026, nous sommes réunis avec fierté et émotion pour célébrer un événement majeur de notre histoire, l'accession de la République de Guinée à l'indépendance. Il y a 68 ans, le peuple de Guinée ouvrait une nouvelle page de son histoire. Cette date demeure profondément gravée dans notre mémoire collective comme un symbole de dignité, de souveraineté et de liberté. Nous rendons hommage à celles et ceux qui, par leur courage, leur engagement et leur détermination, ont contribué à l'avènement de notre indépendance. Leur héritage nous rappelle qu'une nation ne se construit véritablement que lorsque ses filles et fils placent l'intérêt général au-dessus de l'intérêt particulier. Chers compatriotes, célébrer notre indépendance ne signifie pas seulement que nous devons regarder vers le passé, c'est également nous interroger sur la Guinée que nous voulons transmettre aux générations futures. Où êtes-vous, chers jeunesses ? Notre pays dispose des ressources humaines considérables, d'un patrimoine culturel exceptionnel et de nombreuses richesses naturelles. Nous devons également cultiver les valeurs qui fondent notre nation : l'unité, la paix, la tolérance, le respect de la diversité, le travail, la solidarité et le patriotisme. À notre jeunesse, je voudrais adresser un message particulier. Vous êtes à la fois le présent et l'avenir de notre pays. Votre créativité, votre énergie et votre engagement sont indispensables à la transformation de notre pays. Croyez en votre capacité de développer vos compétences, d'entreprendre, d'innover et de participer pleinement à la construction d'une Guinée moderne, prospère et solidaire. » Témoin des premières heures de l’accession de la Guinée à l’indépendance, Elhadj Django Cissé, ancien président de la délégation spéciale de Kindia et secrétaire fédéral du PDG-RDA, a également rendu hommage aux devanciers. « Les trois dates, le 27 août, le 28 septembre et le 2 octobre, sont des trois dates alors qu'ils ont tout donné à la Guinée. Le 27 août, il y a eu l'affrontement de deux grands discours de deux grands leaders. Le 28 septembre, on s'est réunis pour dire non. Et le 2 octobre, on a proclamé notre indépendance que nous sommes en train aujourd'hui de finir. Merci à tout le monde. L'espoir est permis. Je demande à la population guinéenne de mettre la balle à terre. Parce que nous ne méritons pas les jets de pierre. Nous ne méritons pas les brûlures de maison. Nous ne méritons pas les injures et autres. La Guinée est un pays de paix, d'académie, de quiétude. On a donné l'exemple aux pays africains. Le choix de la Guinée en 58 a ramené la Côte d'Ivoire, le Mali, le Niger en 1960 à l'indépendance. Notre pays a un parfait milieu. » La cérémonie s’est achevée dans une ambiance festive avec des prestations artistiques ainsi que des démonstrations de deux écoles de karaté. Un moment de ferveur et de joie partagé par les populations de Kindia à l’occasion de ce 68ᵉ anniversaire de l’indépendance de la Guinée. Aboubacar Dramé, correspondant régional à Kindia +224 623 08 09 10 L’article Kindia : la fête de l’indépendance célébrée sous le signe de la paix et de la solidarité est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Réparations communautaires et collectives des événements de 1991 : Le HCRRUN en mission d’écoute des populations de Dankpen
items.description: Guérin-Kouka, 2 oct. (ATOP) – Le Haut-commissariat à la réconciliation et au renforcement de l’unité nationale (HCRRUN) a organisé, du 29 septembre au 1 er octobre à Guérin-Kouka, une session d’écoute et d’échanges sur l’identification de projets à réaliser dans le cadre des réparations communautaires et collectives suite aux affrontements malheureux survenus en 1991, au profit de la population de Dankpen. Cette démarche s’inscrit dans la mise en œuvre des recommandations de la Commission vérité justice et réconciliation (CVJR), plus précisément sur les réparations communautaires et collectives. La session a pour but d’informer les participants sur le volet réparations communautaires et collectives afin de recueillir leur avis et propositions pour la mise en œuvre des projets d’intérêts communs. Aux termes des échanges, un projet sur la construction d’un centre de formation professionnelle et technique, qui constituera un outil efficace de lutte contre la déscolarisation de la jeunesse a été retenu. Ce centre sera adossé d’un espace de loisirs et de retrouvailles afin de répondre à la double attente des populations de Dankpen. Un accord de mise en œuvre du projet a été signé entre la présidente du HCRRUN, Awa Nana Daboya et le préfet de Dankpen, col. Akpamoura Koffi, représentant les populations concernées. La présidente du HCRRUN, a fait savoir que la recommandation 54 de la CVJR stipule que « malgré les réparations individuelles, tous les conflits intercommunautaires et religieux doivent bénéficier des réparations communautaires et collectives ». Mme Awa Nana Daboya a précisé que dans le cadre de ces réparations, ce sont les populations elles-mêmes qui choisissent un projet fédérateur, conciliateur et au sein duquel elles vont toutes se retrouver pour prôner le vivre-ensemble, la paix et le développement. Le préfet de Dankpen, a témoigné la reconnaissance des populations aux autorités pour cette démarche visant à prôner la paix et la cohésion sociale. Col. Akpamoua a souligné que le projet choisi, est le symbole de leur réconciliation retrouvée. ATOP/BN/BA

items.title: US to raise EB-5 visa fees, new charges take effect Nov 30
items.description: The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) will introduce new fees for the EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program from November 30, 2026. The agency said the fee adjustments are intended to ensure that charges paid by EB-5 applicants cover the cost of administering the programme, while helping USCIS meet statutory processing-time targets and strengthen programme integrity. Congress established the EB-5 programme in 1990 to support U.S. economic growth through foreign investment and job creation. Under the programme, eligible immigrant investors can qualify for lawful permanent residence, commonly known as a Green Card, by investing in the U.S. and creating jobs for American workers. The EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 requires USCIS to conduct a programme-specific fee study and set fees at levels that recover the full cost of administering the programme. The legislation also introduced processing-time targets and strengthened measures designed to protect the integrity of the EB-5 programme. These measures include compliance reviews, audits and site visits, as well as additional safeguards to detect and prevent fraud and abuse. USCIS said it is largely funded through fees paid by people who use the immigration system rather than through taxpayer funding. As a result, the fees collected from applicants help fund activities such as reviewing applications, conducting background checks, verifying eligibility, investigating potential fraud and maintaining programme operations. The new EB-5 fees are scheduled to take effect on November 30, 2026. The final rule follows a notice of proposed rulemaking published by the Department of Homeland Security in October 2025. The EB-5 programme remains one of the employment-based immigration routes through which foreign investors can seek permanent residence in the United States by meeting investment and job-creation requirements. items.title: Chelle makes two changes to Super Eagles squad after Ndidi’s withdrawal
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Super Eagles head coach, Éric Chelle, has made two changes to his squad for Nigeria’s international friendly against Russia following the withdrawals of captain Wilfred Ndidi and defender Akpe Victory. Midfielder John Otomewo and defender Vince Osuji have been called up to replace Ndidi and Akpe respectively, with both players now in line to make their senior international debuts against Russia on Tuesday. Otomewo recently joined French Ligue 2 side Stade de Reims from Israeli Premier League club Hapoel Jerusalem, while Osuji currently plays for Norwegian club Tromsø after leaving Belgian side Club Brugge this summer. The two changes come after Ndidi, who was originally named captain of the 24-man squad, withdrew from the Russia friendly. The reason for his withdrawal has not been officially disclosed. Akpe, who was handed his first senior call-up for the fixture, is also unavailable. Nigeria will face Russia at the Nizhny Novgorod Stadium on Tuesday, October 6, in a friendly Chelle is using to assess players and broaden his options following the Super Eagles’ opening 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying fixtures. Nigeria began the qualifiers with a 2-1 victory over Madagascar in Uyo before suffering a 3-0 defeat to Guinea-Bissau in Bissau. The Super Eagles have also arrived in Russia ahead of the encounter, with the Nigerian delegation reaching Moscow on Friday. Chelle’s original Russia squad included experienced players such as goalkeeper Stanley Nwabali, Moses Simon, Bright Osayi-Samuel, Benjamin Fredrick, Raphael Onyedika and Akor Adams, alongside several players in line for their first senior appearances. Kelechi Iheanacho is also part of the squad after returning to the national team, while the friendly provides an opportunity for Chelle to continue assessing emerging players. Several players in the squad are in line to make their debut, including Ikorodu City’s duo Michael Atata (GK) and midfielder Aderemi Adeoye. Others include Benfica’s forward Peter Edopolor, Hradec Králové’s striker Abdullahi Umar, Fulham’s midfielder Chibuzo Nwoko Nwoko, Basel’s defender Victory Akpe, Slavia Prague’s Suleiman Mubarak, Famalicão’s Abubakar Umar, among others. Nigeria and Russia last met in June 2025, when the Super Eagles held the hosts to a 1-1 draw at Moscow’s Luzhniki Stadium. items.title: Carburant : pour «faire baisser les prix» Macron annonce un plan du G7 pour libérer «jusqu'à 100 millions de barils» de diesel et de pétrole brut
items.description: Les pays du G7 se sont reunis en visioconference ce 2 octobre pour tenter de coordonner leur reponse a la flambee des prix du carburant. a l'issue de cette reunion, presidee par la France, le president Emmanuel Macron a fait savoir que les pays membres allaient liberer « jusqu'a 100 millions de barils » de « diesel et petrole brut », « dans les quatre mois ». Le chef de l'etat francais a egalement indique qu'il n'y aurait « pas d'interdiction » sur les exportations de gazole entre les pays membres du G7, estimant que les decisions prises lors de cette reunion « devraient faire baisser les prix » des carburants et soulager le marche mondial. La decision suit des pressions du president americain, Donald Trump, qui depuis plusieurs jours demande aux pays europeens de puiser dans leurs reserves strategiques de carburant pour freiner la hausse des prix et notamment celle du gazole, sur fond des conflits au Moyen-Orient, de la fermeture du detroit d'Ormuz et des frappes ukrainiennes contre des raffineries russes. « Le processus va commencer immediatement » Sur Truth Social, le president americain a indique que « l'Europe venait d'accepter de mettre sur le marche une quantite massive de son gazole abondamment stocke », assurant que « le processus va commencer immediatement ». Donald Trump avait precedemment evoque l'hypothese de ne plus livrer de diesel americain a l'etranger. Le 1ᵉʳ octobre, Washington a averti qu'une action conjointe avec les etats-Unis sur la question du carburant etait dans « l'interet » de l'Europe, laissant tout de meme planer la menace d'une interdiction des exportations de gazole americain. Une etude de la firme Oxford Economics, specialisee en conseil et en prevision economique, a prevu une flambee allant de 40 a 50 % des prix du diesel en Europe en cas d'execution de ce scenario. a l'heure actuelle, 50 % des importations de gazole de l'Union europeenne (UE) proviennent des etats-Unis. Selon les chiffres d'Eurostat, les reserves de diesel de l'UE s'elevent a pres de 290 millions de barils, dont 21 % sont detenus par la France. Pour sa part, l'Agence internationale de l'energie (AIE) a annonce en mars dernier le deblocage de 400 millions de barils de petrole, fournis a hauteur de 20 % par l'Europe. Cependant, l'integralite de ce volume n'a pas encore ete mise sur le marche : seuls les deux tiers ont ete liberes jusqu'a present, selon les declarations du patron de l'AIE, Fatih Birol.

items.title: Fusaini Yakubu Abanga leads NPP National Youth Organiser race with 45% in Global InfoAnalytics poll
items.description: Fusaini Yakubu Abanga has maintained his lead in the race for National Youth Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), recording 45% in the final wave of a Global InfoAnalytics tracking poll. The survey, conducted between September 24 and 28, 2026, put Clement Opoku Gyamfi on 22%, followed by Michael Osei Boateng with 14%. Alfred Ababio and Vera Oye Bram-Larbi each recorded 7%, while Chris Lloyd Asamoah polled 4%. The figures form part of a three-wave tracking exercise conducted in September, with Abanga’s measured support remaining relatively stable throughout the period. He recorded 46% in the first wave on September 17 before polling 45% in both the September 23 and September 28 surveys. Gyamfi, meanwhile, recorded 30% in the first wave before dropping to 22% in the second wave, where he remained in the final survey. Boateng’s support increased from 9% in the first wave to 14% in the second and final waves. Ababio also recorded an increase, moving from 1% in the first wave to 8% in the second before recording 7% in the final survey. Bram-Larbi moved from 4% initially to 7% in the final wave. Asamoah’s measured support moved in the opposite direction, falling from 9% in the first wave to 4% in the final two surveys. Poll methodology The final survey involved 3,263 NPP delegates across all 16 regions, using the party’s 2026 constituencies register, according to Global InfoAnalytics. The poll was conducted through Computer Assisted Telephone Interviews (CATI), with the organisation reporting a response rate of more than 80% of calls placed. Global InfoAnalytics reported a 98% confidence level and a margin of error of plus or minus 1.35 percentage points. The sample size increased from 2,342 delegates in the first wave on September 17 to 3,288 on September 23 before settling at 3,263 in the final survey. The findings represent measured delegate preferences during the survey period and do not determine the eventual election result. NPP elections The NPP’s National Officers’ Elections are scheduled for Saturday, October 3, at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi. The Electoral Commission is supervising the election, with 7,121 delegates expected to vote and 47 aspirants contesting various national positions. The National Youth Organiser position is among nine national offices being contested.

items.title: ECP proposes holding Punjab local govt elections on Dec 14
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Friday proposed holding local government elections in Punjab on Dec 14 and sent a draft of the suggested schedule to the Punjab chief secretary for consultation. In a letter seen by Dawn , Chaudhry Nadeem Qasim, additional director general for local government elections, forwarded the draft schedule to the Punjab chief secretary on the commission’s behalf. He also sought the provincial government’s opinion on the proposed timelines so that a final schedule could be notified after approval from the ECP. According to the proposed schedule, nomination papers will be filed from Oct 27 to 30, while scrutiny will be conducted from Nov 2 to 5. Appeals against acceptance or rejection of papers can be filed from Nov 7 to 11, and will be decided by tribunals between Nov 12 and 16. As per the letter, the last proposed date for withdrawal of candidature is Nov 18. The final list of candidates will be displayed on Nov 19 and election symbols will be allotted on Nov 20. Polling is proposed for Dec 14, with returning officers to announce results by Dec 17, the letter said. The letter also referred to a consultative meeting held on Aug 20 between the ECP and a provincial cabinet committee on the announcement of the poll date. It is worth noting that during the meeting, the ECP had agreed to the provincial government’s proposal to hold polls between Dec 15 and Jan 15, 2027. On Aug 6, the Punjab cabinet had approved an allocation of Rs12.5 billion for holding local government elections in the province. The last local government elections in Punjab were held in 2015 under the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013. Polling took place in phases between Oct and Dec 2015, and elected councils assumed office in 2017 after indirect elections for mayors and chairpersons. Since then, local body polls in Punjab have experienced repeated delays. The PTI government had dissolved the elected local bodies in April 2019 before they completed their tenure. The move was later struck down by the Supreme Court, which restored them. They eventually completed their term on Dec 31, 2021. Successive provincial governments repeatedly amended or replaced the Punjab Local Government Act. Each legislative change required the ECP to restart preparations, including delimitation and election planning. Changing laws and administrative delays by successive governments contributed significantly to the postponement of the local body elections. Under Article 140A of the Constitution and the Elections Act, local government elections should be held within 120 days of the expiry of local bodies. Since the councils’ term ended in Dec 2021, elections were due by April 2022 but they have been repeatedly postponed.

items.description: Suame Methodist Junior High School has renewed calls for support to strengthen Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education at the school as it marks 120 years of providing quality education. The school’s Head Teacher, Mr. George Tiako, said although the school has the space and facilities to support STEM education, inadequate equipment, particularly computers, remains a major gap that needs urgent attention. “When I took over as the headmaster, I realised there were some gaps. The school has a lot of facilities; they have the space for STEM, but there were only two computers in there which didn’t look like a modern computer lab,” he said. Mr. Tiako made the remarks during the school’s 120th anniversary celebration held on its premises on Friday, September 25, 2026. The celebration was held on the theme, “120 Years of Quality Education: Sustaining the Legacy Through Innovation, Excellence and Godly Values.” He said efforts had since been made to improve the situation, including support from old students who donated 20 desks and 40 chairs.The school has also received GH¢10,000 from another supporter and two additional computers, but Mr. Tiako said more support was needed to fully equip the STEM facility. He also disclosed that the school had introduced a digital system that allows parents to access their wards’ academic reports directly, eliminating the need for students to take hard copies home. Mr. Tiako said his vision was to make Suame Methodist JHS “the hub of education in the municipality.” 120 years of producing notable personalities The school, established in 1906, has produced several prominent personalities who have contributed to Ghana’s development. They include Ghana’s second Prime Minister, Professor Kofi Abrefa Busia; Chief of Staff Julius Debrah; Dr. Matthew Opoku Prempreh; the late highlife musician Daddy Lumba; and Dr. Sampson Antwi of the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital. The anniversary brought together Methodist Church leaders, education authorities, traditional leaders, parents, teachers, old students and other stakeholders to reflect on the school’s achievements and challenges while looking ahead to its next chapter. Bishop Jeremiah Morison of the Kumasi North Diocesan, said the school’s 120-year legacy could only be sustained through innovation. He, however, stressed that technological advancement and academic excellence must be accompanied by strong moral values. “Excellence goes with values,” he said. Bishop Morison urged the school to look beyond producing students with good grades and focus equally on developing students with strong moral character.He also called on parents to become more involved in their children’s education and participate actively in PTA meetings.According to him, parents must take their responsibilities seriously by supporting their children’s education both at home and in school. Education Director calls for collective support The Suame Municipal Director of Education, Mr. Clinton Henaka Budu, said the achievements of the school’s former students demonstrated the quality of education it had provided over the years. “From the dignitaries that have been mentioned here, indeed, the quality of education has produced a lot of people. The least we can do is to maintain the legacy or, better still, build upon it,” he said. Mr. Budu said stakeholders should aim to leave the school in a better condition than they found it. He acknowledged the need for improved infrastructure and said government support would be required for some of the major projects, particularly STEM facilities. He also encouraged other stakeholders to contribute towards addressing immediate needs such as painting and renovation. Old student calls for facelift An old student of the school and Ashanti Regional NDC Organiser, Isham Alhassan, also expressed concern about the physical appearance of the school and called for urgent action to improve its infrastructure. “I’m not pleased with the status of the school after 120 years. I’m going to have meetings with the head of the school to see how best we can help the school,” he said. Mr. Alhassan donated GH¢5,000 towards the development of the school and said arrangements were being made to secure cement to support renovation works. He also indicated plans to engage other prominent old students, including Chief of Staff Julius Debrah, to explore additional support for the school. The Chairman of the anniversary celebration, Evangelist Michael Adu Poku, also announced a donation of two computers to support the school’s STEM agenda. He urged parents to invest in their wards’ education by providing books and other learning materials, stressing the importance of hard work and dedication in achieving educational success. The school’s 120th anniversary has therefore become not only a celebration of its long history and contribution to education but also a renewed call for stakeholders to equip it for the demands of modern education. With support from government, the Methodist Church, old students, parents and other stakeholders, the school hopes to strengthen its STEM facilities while preserving the academic excellence and moral values that have shaped its 120-year legacy

items.title: Doufelgou : la SALT-Niamtougou soutient la scolarisation des élèves démunis
items.description: Niamtougou, 2 oct. (ATOP) – La Société aéroportuaire de Lomé-Tokoin, section de Niamtougou (SALT-Niamtougou) a offert, le jeudi 1 er octobre, des fournitures scolaires aux élèves démunis de quatre Ecoles primaires publiques (EPP) de la commune Doufelgou 1. Remise symbolique Les bénéficiaires sont issus des EPP Kirga, Founougou, Centrale et Yaka respectivement dans les cantons de Baga, Koka, Niamtougou, et d’Agbandé-Yaka. Le don est composé de cahiers, de stylos, ainsi que de boîtes de craie blanche. L’initiative vise à soutenir la scolarisation des enfants vulnérables et à alléger les charges des familles. Le préfet de Doufelgou, Col. Aziaba Ayi Sessi a salué l’engagement social et citoyen de la SALT-Niamtougou, qu’il a présenté comme une contribution à la promotion d’une éducation inclusive. Il a souligné que cette action permet aux enfants issus de familles démunies de disposer de matériel scolaire pour poursuivre leur apprentissage dans de meilleures conditions. Le préfet a félicité les enseignants pour leur dévouement et les a exhortés à redoubler d’efforts afin de contribuer à la formation d’une jeunesse dynamique et capable de relever les défis de demain. La remise s’est déroulée en présence du secrétaire préfectoral de l’Union pour la République (UNIR), Boya Wenberma Martin, de la coordinatrice et point focal de l’ONG Aide et action à la veuve, à l’orphelin et à l’enfant déshérité, Mme Awata Jacqueline, ainsi que des chefs traditionnels des cantons concernés, des représentants des forces de défense et de sécurité. ATOP/SG/TAL/MD

items.title: 5 countries to buy iPhone 18 Pro cheaper in 2026
items.description: Apple’s latest iPhone 18 Pro has different prices depending on where it is purchased, with taxes, exchange rates and regional pricing contributing to significant differences between markets. For Nigerians looking to buy the iPhone 18 Pro abroad, several countries currently offer lower official Apple prices than many other major markets. Apple launched the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max in September 2026, with the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro starting at $1,199 in the United States. Based on Apple’s official prices and current international price comparisons, these are five markets worth considering. 1. United States The United States has the lowest advertised starting price for the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro among the major markets compared. Apple lists the device at $1,199 before applicable state and local sales taxes. This means the final amount paid at checkout can be higher depending on the state where the phone is purchased. The US price is also the benchmark against which prices in other countries are commonly compared. However, buyers travelling from Nigeria should remember that the advertised US price does not necessarily represent the final cost because of sales tax and other travel-related expenses. 2. Canada Canada is another relatively low-cost market for the iPhone 18 Pro. Apple’s Canadian price for the 256GB model is C$1,749. International price comparisons put this at roughly US$1,230–$1,310, depending on the exchange rate and whether taxes are included in the comparison. The final amount paid can vary because Canadian provinces apply different sales taxes. 3. Malaysia Malaysia also features among the cheaper markets for Apple’s latest Pro iPhone. The 256GB iPhone 18 Pro is priced at RM5,499 in Malaysia. Current international comparisons put that at approximately US$1,348. This puts Malaysia ahead of several major markets in terms of the advertised converted price. 4. United Arab Emirates The UAE, particularly Dubai, is another market Nigerians often consider when shopping for Apple products. Apple lists the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro from AED5,099 in the UAE. That is approximately US$1,388 at current exchange rates. The UAE’s 5% VAT is already reflected in Apple’s consumer pricing, although eligible tourists may be able to claim a VAT refund under the country’s tourist tax-refund system. The UAE is therefore one of the more competitive options for Nigerians who are already travelling to Dubai or Abu Dhabi. 5. Japan Japan completes the five markets in this comparison. Apple’s Japanese store lists the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro at ¥219,800, including consumption tax. That works out to roughly US$1,397, although the exact dollar equivalent will change with exchange rates. Japan therefore remains relatively competitive compared with markets such as the UK, India and several European countries. Note: The rate is at the time of publishing the article. items.title: Alleged cybercrime: Prosecution faults Sowore’s insistence on DSS DG testimony
items.description: The prosecution in the trial of Omoyele Sowore, publisher of Sahara Reporters, on Friday faulted the insistence by the defence that the Director General (DG) of the Department of State Services (DSS), Tosin Ajayi, must appear in person to testify as a Defence witness. The Prosecution Counsel, Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, argued that it was wrong for Sowore’s lawyer, Adeyinka Olumide-Fusika, SAN, to insist that the DG, DSS, must attend court in person to testify as a subpoenaed witness of the defence. Kehinde made the position known at the resumed hearing of the case before Justice Mohammed Umar of the Federal High Court in Abuja. It would be recalled that Sowore, the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), is being prosecuted by the DSS on allegations bordering on cybercrime. The defendant was alleged to have, in August 2025, published posts on X (formerly Twitter) and Facebook, describing President Bola Tinubu as a “criminal” and accusing him of lying about the level of corruption in the country. Kehinde, while presenting his argument, cited a Supreme Court’s decision in the case of Ishaq v. Soniyi (2002) ALL FWLR part 498, page 347 at 373. He submitted that the apex court held that where a subpoena is directed to a named official, it will be absurd to insist that only the named officer is to appear in due compliance with the subpoena. Kehinde recalled that the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) attended court on July 28, leading the prosecution’s team, to make the same point that it was wrong for the defence to insist that the DG must testify as its witness in person. He said it was based on that understanding that parties agreed that an official of the DSS should be nominated to stand in for the boss. The prosecuting lawyer told the court that, in fidelity to that understanding, an official of the DSS was designated for that purpose. He said the said official was present in court and was ready for the business of the day. He added that the DSS boss has no personal interest in the case and only acted in an official capacity. He stressed that since the DSS had cases in the various divisions of the FHC, it was practically impossible to expect him to attend all proceedings. “This case is over a year old. The prosecution closed its case on March 16, 2026. “It is not an act of charity on the part of the defence to argue that, at a point, it agreed that an official of the DSS should come, but now it is insisting on the DG alone. “The decision as to who should attend court is at the discretion of the court, not that of the defence. “An official of the DSS is competent to give evidence in place of the DG,” Kehinde said. Earlier, Olumide-Fusika had claimed that the prosecution had repudiated the understanding by parties that an official of the DSS should attend court in the place of its DG by allegedly failing to produce the said official on the last date. The lawyer argued that since the name on the subpoena and the hearing notice issued was that of the DG, he must attend court in person. He said the decision to issue a subpoena on the DG in his personal capacity was necessitated by the fact that the 2nd defence witness, Uwem Davies, an official of the DSS, had, while testifying, kept saying that it was the only DG who could answer some of the questions put to him. Justice Umar subsequently adjourned the matter until Oct. 6 for ruling on whether or not the DG can be compelled to appear in person and testify as a defence witness in respect of actions taken by the agency. (NAN) The post Alleged cybercrime: Prosecution faults Sowore’s insistence on DSS DG testimony appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Global fashion coalition launches in the heart of Kantamanto Market
items.description: Kantamanto Obroniwawu Businesses Association (KOBA), the unified association of market section leaders, have welcomed representatives from four of the world’s largest fashion companies to Kantamanto Market for the launch of the Apparel Recovery Coalition (ARC). Co-founded by H&M Group, Inditex, BESTSELLER, adidas, The Or Foundation and supported by Circle Economy as an independent facilitator, ARC aims to explore how producer responsibility systems can support circular pathways such as reuse, upcycling, recycling, and responsible waste management in countries that receive large volumes of exported secondhand apparel, such as Ghana. Speaking at the launch Reverend Opoku Afreh, President of Kantamanto Obroniwawu Businesses Association said, ”Our expectation is that ARC will build upon the existing knowledge, skills and resourcefulness of the Kantamanto community rather than overlook or replace them. We want our members to have access to the necessary infrastructure, investment and opportunities to expand their businesses, improve their livelihoods and strengthen the sustainable practices they have developed over decades.” The launch took place at the heart of Accra’s Kantamanto Market, one of the world’s largest hubs for secondhand clothing reuse, repair, and upcycling. The market recirculates 25 million garments each month while supporting the livelihoods of tens of thousands of workers and entrepreneurs. At this scale, Kantamanto offers a valuable lens for understanding how post-consumer textiles are managed, as well as the growing environmental and social impacts associated with them, such as water and soil pollution. Staged within Kantamanto Market’s central Egg Sellers Lane, guests sat under upcycled canopies made by The Or Foundation’s Remanufactory with a podium and sound system made from Cassaboard, a material developed by The Or Foundation’s Material Technology and Transformation Lab made from waste textiles. “I thank the Kantamanto Obroni Wawu Businesses Association – KOBA – and The Or Foundation for inviting the Presidency to this market, not a hotel conference room, but here, where the real work happens”, Mr. Afreh noted. Speaking on behalf of Dr Julius Debrah, Chief of Staff, Deputy Presidential Spokesperson, Shamima Muslim said, “This is a monumental step. For the first time, big brands are coming to Kantamanto not to take pictures but to acknowledge communities like Kantamanto have kept global fashion circular, and that they must pay their fair share.” Addressing the brand representatives, Gifty Anderson, Secretary of Kantamanto Women’s Association said “Normally these decisions are made from boardrooms overseas leaving us to deal with the impacts of those decisions. But you have come to us, first to see with your own eyes what we have been dealing with. This is a small but important step to delivering the justice that we need. We must acknowledge the problem before we can begin to find a solution.” Today, producer responsibility systems are largely tied to the primary markets where products are first sold, while many post-consumer textiles move across borders, and their impacts are felt elsewhere. According to the European Environment Agency, for example, around 1.4 million metric tons of used textiles are exported from the EU annually, mainly to countries in Africa and Asia. Over the next two years, ARC will build and test a producer responsibility blueprint that reflects the global nature of post-consumer textile flows, engaging brands, producer responsibility organisations, sorters, recyclers, policymakers and affected communities to help shape practical solutions. As its first demonstration project, ARC will explore how producer responsibility contributions can help strengthen Ghana’s existing circular textile ecosystem. The Coalition recognises the work The Or Foundation has done over the past 15 years to support this ecosystem, and it aims to build on that experience while learning from the communities at the heart of the secondhand clothing trade. Through the demonstration project, The Or Foundation will continue to organise and implement initiatives across Accra, such as improvements to infrastructure at Kantamanto Market, environmental remediation, and training programmes.

items.title: La BAD, le Fonds de l’OPEP et les Pays-Bas renforcent les sauvegardes environnementales et sociales en Afrique
items.description: Vienne, Autriche, 1 Octobre 2026 — Plus de 50 représentants de pays africains et d’institutions de financement du développement étaient réunis la semaine dernière à Vienne pour renforcer les systèmes de gestion des risques environnementaux et sociaux dans les projets de développement. Cette réunion se déroulait dans le cadre d’une initiative de renforcement des capacités menée par le Groupe de la Banque africaine de développement et le Fonds de l’OPEP pour le développement international. L’atelier de trois jours, organisé par l’institution panafricaine, le Fonds de l’OPEP (OFID) et la Commission néerlandaise pour l’évaluation environnementale (NCEA), a marqué la seconde phase de l’initiative de renforcement des capacités environnementales et sociales (E&S) de la Banque et de l’OFID, lancée en juin 2025 à Vienne (Autriche). De hauts responsables des autorités de régulation africaines (Tchad, Comores, RDC, Kenya, Madagascar, Niger, Sénégal et Ouganda) ont participé à l’atelier. Étaient également présents des représentants d’institutions internationales : Banque mondiale, Banque islamique de développement, Banque asiatique d’investissement pour les infrastructures, BERD, BADEA, Fonds saoudien pour le développement, Fonds d’Abu Dhabi pour le développement, Fonds arabe pour le développement économique et social, Private Infrastructure Development Group, UNESCO, ainsi que les cabinets de conseil en environnement Alpage et Ramboll. Lors de tables rondes et de présentations d’études de cas, les participants ont examiné les questions suivantes : l’acquisition de terres et la réinstallation ; la biodiversité ; l’inclusion sociale ; les violences sexistes et l’exploitation sexuelle ; les abus et le harcèlement ; le patrimoine culturel ; la santé et la sécurité au travail et au sein des communautés. Ils ont également étudié différentes approches en matière de financement et de suivi des plans de gestion environnementale et sociale, ainsi que de renforcement de la coopération entre les institutions financières et les autorités de régulation nationales. Cette initiative s’appuie sur les évaluations des systèmes environnementaux et sociaux nationaux réalisées par la Banque africaine de développement dans différents pays du continent (Bénin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Tchad, Comores, Côte d’Ivoire, RDC, Érythrée, Gabon, Gambie, Madagascar, Mali, Mauritanie, Maroc, Niger, Nigéria, Sénégal, Sierra Leone, Soudan du Sud, Togo, Tunisie et Ouganda). « Les mesures de sauvegarde environnementales et sociales ne constituent pas un élément accessoire du développement ; elles font partie intégrante d’un développement plus durable, plus inclusif et plus équitable, a déclaré Musab Alomar, vice-président du Fonds de l’OPEP chargé de la stratégie. Veiller à ce que les projets que nous finançons respectent des normes environnementales et sociales rigoureuses est une responsabilité partagée et une pierre angulaire d’un développement efficace. » Selon Maman-Sani Issa, directeur des sauvegardes environnementales et sociales et de la conformité du Groupe de la Banque, partenariat offre aux pays des opportunités concrètes d’échanger leurs expériences et de renforcer leurs capacités nationales. « L’objectif est de doter nos pays membres régionaux des connaissances et des compétences pratiques nécessaires pour intégrer les considérations environnementales et sociales dans la conception et la mise en œuvre des projets, a-t-il indiqué. Des systèmes nationaux plus solides contribueront à améliorer l’utilisation durable et la préservation du capital naturel et humain dans l’ensemble de nos pays membres ; ce qui renforcera, à terme, la durabilité et l’impact sur le développement des projets que nous soutenons. » La NCEA a animé un groupe de discussion permettant aux représentants des pays et aux institutions financières multilatérales de discuter de la manière de financer le suivi des plans de gestion environnementale et sociale, ainsi que de la façon dont ces institutions peuvent collaborer avec les autorités de régulation pour renforcer le suivi et la conformité. Dennis van Peppen, directeur de la Commission néerlandaise pour l’évaluation environnementale, a souligné l’importance de cet atelier en tant que plateforme d’apprentissage par les pairs et de dialogue sur les défis et les opportunités liés au renforcement des systèmes environnementaux et sociaux nationaux. Durant ces trois jours, l’équipe du Groupe de la Banque africaine de développement a également mené des discussions avec ses partenaires sur le cofinancement et le renforcement des capacités, entre autres sujets. La prochaine phase de l’initiative devrait inclure des formations sur mesure au niveau national, conçues pour répondre aux défis spécifiques à chaque pays et renforcer davantage les systèmes de sauvegarde environnementale et sociale comme fondements d’une mise en œuvre durable des projets. À propos du Fonds de l’OPEP pour le développement international : Le Fonds de l’OPEP est la seule institution de développement dotée d’un mandat mondial qui octroie des financements provenant de ses pays membres exclusivement à des pays non membres. Le Fonds collabore avec des pays en développement partenaires et la communauté internationale du développement afin de stimuler la croissance économique et de réduire la pauvreté. À propos de la Commission néerlandaise pour l’évaluation environnementale La Commission néerlandaise pour l’évaluation environnementale conseille et apporte son soutien aux gouvernements, organisations et institutions du monde entier dans l’évaluation des impacts potentiels sur les populations et l’environnement dans le cadre de processus décisionnels majeurs. Contact médias : Frédéric Bambara, Département de la communication et des relations extérieures, Groupe de la Banque africaine de développement | courriel : media@afdb.org L’article La BAD, le Fonds de l’OPEP et les Pays-Bas renforcent les sauvegardes environnementales et sociales en Afrique est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Man City whistleblower Rui Pinto facing ‘dire consequences’ – Lawyers
items.description: Computer hacker Rui Pinto, the man behind the Football Leaks website which helped trigger the Premier League probe into Manchester City’s finances, faces “dire consequences” after having his protected witness status removed, his lawyers said on Friday. Pinto “was informed on Wednesday that the special security programme he has benefited from since August 2020 would end on October 10,” his Portuguese lawyers Francisco and Luisa Teixeira da Mota said in a joint statement with his French representatives William Bourdon and Vincent Brengarth. “In a few days, without having been given a prior hearing as required by law, he would lose the secure, confidential housing assigned to him and be forced to find a new home urgently, with no guarantee that police protection would be maintained,” they continued, describing the move as a “decision with dire consequences”. “The threats against him are not merely theoretical; he was assaulted in Lisbon last April. His revelations implicated powerful figures with vast resources, and numerous resulting legal proceedings are still ongoing,” they noted. “Abruptly deprived of his protected housing and plunged into extreme precariousness, Rui Pinto is reportedly more vulnerable now than at any time since 2020,” his lawyers added. The 37-year-old Pinto has been a protected witness since 2020 after agreeing to grant Portuguese authorities access to millions of files gathered before his arrest. Arrested in Hungary where he was living in January 2019 and subsequently extradited to his home country Portugal, Pinto spent over a year in pre-trial detention before agreeing to cooperate with authorities by granting them access to the encrypted data in his possession. Pinto was both a defendant and a protected witness for the Portuguese justice system. He is also cooperating with investigators from other European countries. During his first trial, the former history student and self-taught computer expert, admitted hacking computers to obtain millions of documents which he began publishing online in late 2015. Passed on to a consortium of European investigative media outlets, this wealth of information exposed questionable practices involving star football players, clubs and agents, subsequently leading to tax adjustments and judicial investigations in several countries. A Portuguese court handed Pinto a suspended four-year sentence in September 2023 after he was found guilty on counts of attempted extortion, illegal access to data and breach of correspondence. items.title: 2027: Gombe parties intensify grassroots mobilisation
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe GOMBE — Political activities are gathering momentum in Gombe State ahead of the 2027 general elections, with parties and aspirants increasingly engaging voters through empowerment programmes, stakeholder meetings, defections, consultations and other grassroots activities. Although many of the events are presented as party-building, community outreach or empowerment initiatives, the participation of political aspirants, party leaders and supporters has given them a growing political dimension as parties position themselves for the 2027 elections. The All Progressives Congress (APC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), African Democratic Congress (ADC) and other political parties are strengthening their structures across the state’s 11 local government areas. Recent developments have particularly heightened activity around the governorship contest. The APC adopted Dr Jamilu Isyaku Gwamna as its consensus governorship candidate for 2027 at an enlarged stakeholders’ meeting in May. The party also adopted consensus candidates for the National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections. The PDP, meanwhile, has concluded another phase of its internal contest following a court-ordered rerun of its governorship primary. A Federal High Court in Gombe had, on September 24, nullified the party’s earlier primary that produced former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Pantami, and ordered a fresh exercise. The PDP subsequently conducted the fresh primary on September 29, with Pantami, Khamisu Ahmed Mailantarki and Usman Aliyu Garry participating. Pantami emerged as the party’s candidate after the rerun, although reports differed on the vote figures announced by different media outlets. Vanguard reported that Pantami polled 2,024 votes, while other reports put his total at 2,054. Mailantarki was reported to have scored 389 votes and Garry 112. With the rerun, Pantami has secured the PDP ticket through a fresh voting process, subject to any further legal or electoral developments. Defections reshape political alignments The political realignment has also been reflected in defections involving prominent figures. In September, former ADC governorship aspirant for the Gombe/Kwami/Funakaye Federal Constituency, Alhaji Mohammed Danjuma, popularly known as Garkuwa Babba, defected to the APC and handed over his political structure to the party. Danjuma, who was a former ADC aspirant for the federal constituency and chairman of the party’s House of Representatives Aspirants Forum, declared his support for the APC’s candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. The movement of political figures between parties has become a feature of preparations for the next election cycle, with defectors often seeking to retain or transfer their existing political networks. Empowerment and grassroots mobilisation Another feature of the emerging political season is the use of empowerment programmes and community engagements by politicians and political groups. Such activities include the distribution of working tools, financial assistance, business support and programmes targeted at youths, women, traders and other community groups. While empowerment programmes may serve social or economic purposes, their political significance can also depend on their timing, organisers and the political figures involved. The events provide opportunities for politicians to interact directly with communities, meet local leaders and strengthen relationships with grassroots organisations. Similarly, stakeholder meetings, consultations and community visits can provide platforms for political messaging and mobilisation ahead of the elections. Parties strengthen structures Beyond the governorship contest, politicians seeking seats in the Senate, House of Representatives and State Houses of Assembly are also expected to strengthen their networks at ward and local government levels. Meetings involving party officials, traditional and community leaders, youth and women groups and other political associations are becoming more prominent as the parties prepare their grassroots structures. The importance of such structures was illustrated by the September 19 Gombe/Kwami/Funakaye Federal Constituency bye-election. APC candidate Usman Maijama’a Kallamu won the contest with 41,121 votes. The election was conducted across 903 polling units in 31 registration areas covering Gombe, Kwami and Funakaye local government areas. The result has provided the parties with another recent electoral outcome to assess their organisation and support across the constituency. APC, PDP positions The APC’s adoption of Gwamna has provided the party with an early governorship candidate around whom it has begun consolidating its political structure. The PDP’s selection of Pantami, meanwhile, follows a more contested path, beginning with his movement from the APC to the PDP and his initial emergence as the opposition party’s candidate before the Federal High Court ordered a fresh primary. Pantami’s emergence from the rerun now places him and Gwamna among the principal figures around whom the two major parties are organising their governorship campaigns, while the ADC and other parties continue to seek space in the contest. Issues likely to shape contest As political activity increases, attention is also likely to shift from party movements and personalities to issues affecting residents of the state. These include employment and youth development, education, healthcare, agriculture, infrastructure, security, poverty reduction, local economic development and the quality of public services. The parties and their candidates will consequently face pressure to explain their programmes and how they intend to address these challenges. For voters, the growing number of political meetings, empowerment programmes, defections and consultations provides an opportunity to examine the competing messages and distinguish between mobilisation activities and specific policy proposals. With the major parties already activating their structures, Gombe’s political landscape is entering a more active phase ahead of the 2027 elections. The formal election period remains ahead, but grassroots political mobilisation and positioning are already becoming increasingly visible across the state. items.title: Ouagadougou : Un centre féminin de formation aux métiers du textile inauguré à Tampouy pour 200 millions de F CFA
items.description: Le Centre féminin de formation aux métiers du textile de Tampouy a été inauguré ce 2 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Ce centre, situé dans l’arrondissement 3, a été réhabilité et équipé pour une valeur de 200 millions de francs CFA. Dans la stratégie de pérennisation des actions de la sous-composante « appui au développement de l’artisanat féminin », le centre féminin de formation aux métiers du textile de Tampouy a été réhabilité et équipé pour servir de vivier pour le transfert de compétences aux futures générations d’apprenantes des métiers du textile. L’inauguration dudit centre a eu lieu ce vendredi 2 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Selon le 2ᵉ vice-président de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Ouagadougou, Boukary Savadogo, représentant le PDS, Maurice Konaté, les attentes sont énormes. « Ce que nous attendons, c’est que ce centre ne soit pas vide un seul instant. Il y a 600 femmes formées, le centre renaît de ses cendres, il faut l’occuper. Il faut toujours travailler », a-t-il dit. Selon le 2ᵉ vice-président de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Ouagadougou, Boukary Savadogo, représentant le PDS Maurice Konaté, les attentes sont énormes. Pour Valentin Bayiri, coordonnateur du projet d’appui au Grand Ouaga, le sens de ce centre est de valoriser le patrimoine culturel burkinabè, de travailler à valoriser davantage la dignité de la femme et de lui donner des atouts qui contribueront à son épanouissement et, à son tour, au développement de la nation. « À travers ce projet, nous mettons en œuvre les directives au niveau national qui nous demandent de faire des offensives, et nous avons fait ici l’offensive dans le domaine de l’artisanat, dans le domaine de la promotion de la femme, de sorte que les femmes du Grand Ouaga puissent réellement bénéficier de compétences et de savoirs pour pouvoir mieux s’épanouir et contribuer au bien-être de leur famille », a-t-il affirmé. Pour Valentin Bayiri, coordonnateur du projet d’appui au Grand Ouaga, le sens de ce centre est de valoriser le patrimoine culturel burkinabè. Dans le but de répondre à la vocation du centre, un appel à candidatures a été lancé pour la sélection de cinquante (50) auditrices pour une formation de longue durée devant aboutir à l’obtention de Certificats de Qualification Professionnelle (CQP). La réhabilitation et l’équipement du centre ont été financés par l’Union européenne. Selon la cheffe de partenariat, Inga Stefanowicz, cette inauguration vient couronner l’activité d’appui à l’artisanat féminin du Projet d’appui à la croissance économique urbaine du Grand Ouaga. « L’Union européenne, partenaire de longue date du Burkina Faso, soutiendra toujours l’autonomisation des femmes, car nous sommes convaincus que soutenir les femmes, c’est soutenir les familles, soutenir la santé, l’éducation des enfants, l’entrepreneuriat, en un mot, le développement socio-économique », a-t-elle déclaré. Selon la cheffe de partenariat, Inga Stefanowicz, cette inauguration vient couronner l’activité d’appui à l’artisanat féminin du Projet d’appui à la croissance économique urbaine du Grand Ouaga. La production des femmes est économique. C’est pourquoi des boutiques ont été mises en place afin qu’elles puissent exposer leurs productions. Ce centre très étoffé et doté de machines performantes, permettra aux femmes de réaliser des productions de qualité, de répondre aux besoins de commandes de grande quantité et d’exporter leurs productions. Il faut noter que la réhabilitation et l'équipement du Centre féminin de formation aux métiers du textile de Tampouy ont été prévus dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre des activités de la sous-composante «Appui au développement de l’artisanat féminin » du Projet d’Appui à la croissance économique urbaine et à la Gouvernance métropolitaine du Grand Ouaga (PAGO). L’article Ouagadougou : Un centre féminin de formation aux métiers du textile inauguré à Tampouy pour 200 millions de F CFA est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: ‘No concrete commitments from government’ – Brong Ahafo teacher unions maintain strike
items.description: Teacher unions in the Brong Ahafo Region have reaffirmed their participation in the ongoing nationwide industrial action, saying they will remain on strike until government provides what they described as “concrete commitments” to address their outstanding concerns. The Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and Pre-Tertiary Teachers’ Association of Ghana (PRETAG) in the Brong Ahafo Region said discussions with the Ministry of Education (MoE) ended without an agreement on the issues that triggered the industrial action. In a statement issued on Thursday, October 1, the three unions said a meeting with Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu on Monday, September 28, failed to produce firm commitments and definite timelines for resolving their concerns. “The Ministry was unable to provide firm commitments and definite timelines for resolving the issues raised by the Teacher Unions,” they stated, adding that the nationwide industrial action declared by their national leadership on September 25 therefore remains in force. At the centre of the dispute is the delay in negotiating a new Collective Agreement for teachers. The unions said negotiations, which should have been completed by June 2026, are still outstanding, describing the delay as a matter of serious concern and calling for the process to be concluded. The unions are also demanding the automatic placement of teachers who sat for aptitude tests in December 2025 and February 2026. According to them, the affected teachers are yet to be automatically placed despite having gone through the required process. They said the delay has created uncertainty among the teachers and called for the matter to be resolved without further delay. Another issue is the implementation of the deprived-area allowance,ce with the unions accusing the MoE of failing to review the Deprived Area Report and negotiate the relevant figures with the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) for implementation as required under Section 17(2) of the 2024 Collective Agreement. The three unions said the lack of concrete commitments and timelines from the Ministry has compelled them to maintain the industrial action. They have consequently urged their members in the Brong Ahafo Region to remain united, peaceful and disciplined throughout the strike. “The strike remains in force and shall continue until the outstanding demands of the Teacher Unions are satisfactorily addressed,” they said, calling on the government and the MoE to engage them with the urgency required to reach a mutually acceptable resolution. They stressed that the industrial action is not intended to undermine education but to push for the implementation of agreed provisions and address concerns affecting teachers. “Rather, it is aimed at securing the implementation of agreed provisions, addressing legitimate concerns of teachers and ensuring a fair and sustainable working environment for teachers and the effective delivery of quality pre-tertiary education,” the unions said. The regional leadership also appealed for continued understanding from parents, guardians, students, traditional authorities, civil society organisations and the general public as negotiations over the outstanding issues continue. The statement was signed by Eric Adongo, Regional Secretary of GNAT Brong Ahafo; Sulley Nyisina, Chairman of NAGRAT Brong Ahafo; and Augusta Amponsah, Chairperson of PRETAG Brong Ahafo.

items.title: Engagement politique des femmes : Un webinaire réunit les élues du Togo, du Bénin et leurs partenaires du Grand Est en France
items.description: Sokodé, 2 oct. (ATOP) – Un webinaire d’échanges sur le thème « Femmes et engagement politique local : expériences croisées et leviers d’action » a réuni, le lundi 28 septembre, des femmes élues du Togo, du Bénin et leurs partenaires de la Région Grand Est en France. Le webinaire a été organisé par la Région Grand Est dans le cadre de sa coopération décentralisée avec la région Centrale au Togo et les Départements de Borgou et de l’Alibori au Bénin. Il s’intègre dans le projet « Appui à la régionalisation et au renforcement de la gouvernance locale et de la décentralisation » . Les participants Les échanges ont vu la participation des représentantes de la Région Grand Est ; ceux de Gescod ; des élus de la région Centrale ; des membres de l’Association des femmes élues locales de la région Centrale du Togo (AFeLORCeT) et des membres de l’Union des femmes conseillères communales des départements de l’Alibori, de l’Atacora, du Borgou, des Collines et de la Donga du Bénin (UFeC/2ABCD). D’autres personnalités y ont été invitées en fonction de leur intérêt pour la thématique. Le webinaire a permis de créer un espace de dialogue et d’apprentissage mutuel contribuant à renforcer la participation et la prise de responsabilités des femmes dans la vie politique locale. La rencontre a servi de cadre pour présenter les missions, le fonctionnement et les priorités de l’AFeLORCeT et pour faire connaître l’expérience de l’UFeC/2ABCD. Elle a permis aux femmes élues de partager leurs parcours, leurs expériences dans l’exercice de leur mandat, les difficultés rencontrées et les stratégies mises en œuvre pour prendre part pleinement à la vie politique locale. Le webinaire a donné lieu à l’identification des principaux freins à la participation et à la prise de responsabilités des femmes dans les institutions locales. Les échanges ont mis en lumière les leviers, pratiques et solutions susceptibles de favoriser une gouvernance locale plus inclusive. L’approche participative a été privilégiée durant les travaux, laissant ainsi une place importante aux témoignages, aux regards croisés, aux questions et à l’identification collective de pistes d’actions. M. Kalessou en pleine intervention durant ce webinaire Le président du conseil régional, Kalessou Kwakou, a souhaité la multiplication de ces genres d’opportunités pour un ancrage politique des femmes élues de la région. La présidente de l’AFeLORCeT, Mme Tchagnao Sourou Ladi a relevé la nécessité pour les femmes élues de continuer à se former pour relever les défis pour plus d’engagement politique. Elle a appelé les jeunes filles à poursuivre leurs études et les femmes à adhérer aux partis politiques et surtout à être des militantes engagées pour le développement de leurs communautés. Le responsable de Gescod-Togo, Ouronilé Adam Daouda a confié que malgré l’accroissement progressif du taux de femmes dans les instances locales, leur accès effectif aux responsabilités, leur participation aux prises de décision et l’exercice de leurs mandats demeurent encore un défi. ATOP/MEK/HKM/BV

items.title: Court jails woman six months for abusing 14-year-old niece
items.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka OWERRI — A Chief Magistrate’s Court in Imo State has sentenced Rose Okon to six months’ imprisonment for assaulting her 14-year-old niece who was in her care. Chief Magistrate C. J. Nkwoada handed down the sentence on Friday after Okon pleaded guilty to a one-count charge of assault. The court, however, gave her an option of N50,000 fine. According to the charge sheet, Okon committed the offence on September 19 at Umuneke, Ngor Okpala, in the Ngor Okpala Magisterial District. The charge alleged that she assaulted the teenager by pouring hot water on her head and body, causing her grievous harm. The charge was brought under Section 355 of the Criminal Code, Cap. C38, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004, as applicable in Imo State. During the proceedings, prosecution counsel, Sampson Obodo, presented photographs showing the injuries sustained by the girl and tendered statements made to the police by the accused and the victim. A statement from the Stand For Humanity Foundation, the organisation that petitioned the police over the incident, was also tendered before the court. After Okon was convicted, the court invited her to make a plea in mitigation before sentencing. Okon pleaded for mercy, while her counsel, Innocent Onyekwere, urged the court to temper justice with mercy. Okon was arrested following a petition by the Stand For Humanity Foundation. Speaking to journalists after the proceedings, the foundation’s president, Chidiebube Okeoma, said the organisation initiated the petition and arrest process to draw attention to the legal consequences of child abuse. Okeoma, a journalist and child-rights advocate, said the conviction should serve as a reminder that child abuse is punishable under Nigerian law. He said the foundation would continue its advocacy against child abuse in Imo State. Okeoma added that the organisation had organised awareness campaigns against child abuse in Owerri on July 4 and September 12, 2026. He said the campaigns involved the Imo State Police Command, the Owerri branch of the Nigerian Bar Association, the Imo State chapter of the Nigeria Medical Association, Nollywood actors and rights activists, among others.
