items.title: Mexico to prohibit presidents from holding dual citizenship
items.description: A Mexican constitutional reform to require presidential candidates to renounce any dual citizenship is fast-tracking toward final approval, despite criticism that the measure backed by the ruling party infringes on political rights and aims to block opposition rivals. President Claudia Sheinbaum has defended the initiative, which would also apply to state governors and the Mexico City mayor as a safeguard against foreign interference. “Presidents of Mexico can only have one flag, one homeland, one people to defend,” Sheinbaum said during her daily news conference on Wednesday. Its critics, however, say it erects hurdles for dual-national politicians and could hamper generational succession within Sheinbaum’s ruling Morena party and those of its allies, where several figures hold foreign passports. The constitutional changes were swiftly approved this week by a majority of Mexico’s 32 state legislatures, backed by Morena lawmakers and their coalition after passing both chambers of the national Congress. Lawmakers must now issue a formal “declaration of constitutionality” before publishing the text in the official gazette. Mexico’s current constitution does not explicitly bar presidents and governors from holding dual citizenship. In Latin America, only two countries have such bans: Cuba and Venezuela. The United States allows dual citizens to become president, but the issue has proven politically sensitive. Ted Cruz renounced his Canadian citizenship in 2014 ahead of his 2016 presidential run. Patriotism or political subterfuge? Sheinbaum and her administration say that the citizenship proposal is part of the party’s broader emphasis on defending national sovereignty amid mounting pressure from the administration of US President Donald Trump. But its critics have questioned both the speed of its passage and its political intentions ahead of the 2030 presidential election. The requirement would take effect for prospective candidates in 2028, meaning it would not affect current state governors or candidates competing in the 2027 midterms. Sheinbaum’s office did not respond to requests for comment. Mexican billionaire Ricardo Salinas, a prominent tycoon and fierce critic of the administration who has repeatedly hinted at political ambitions, has railed against the bill and suggested that it was designed specifically to thwart his possible run. “Are they willing to screw over millions of Mexicans who migrated north… solely out of a sick desire to block a Mexican whom they fear and hate from the presidency?” Salinas wrote in a social media post in August. On Monday, Salinas appeared to reverse course, writing on social media that he did not hold dual citizenship; Reuters could not confirm whether he holds a second citizenship. A spokesperson for Grupo Salinas declined to comment, describing his citizenship status as a private matter. A source within the Morena party, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters the reform was aimed at hampering a possible run by Salinas. Larry Rubin, president of the American Society of Mexico, who holds dual US and Mexican citizenship, has also condemned the measure. “Having two nationalities does not make anyone less Mexican,” Rubin said. “Do not turn your back on millions of dual nationals, migrants, and binational families.” Mexican ambassador to the United States, Roberto Lazzeri, however, said the measure is not a referendum on dual citizenship, but rather a specific tightening of the requirements for the highest political offices. “Holding dual nationality does not make anyone less Mexican,” he wrote on social media on Tuesday, though he added, “the greater the public responsibility, the greater the obligations toward the country.”

items.title: Citizenship-by-investment: EU deadline throws Nigerian golden passport holders into uncertainty
items.description: … EU, UK others toeing Trump’s stringent immigration stance – Foreign policy expert … Calls for domestic policy reset … Focus may be shifted to residency schemes in Malta, Greece, others – Migration advisory firm By Nkiruka Nnorom Thousands of wealthy Nigerians who once turned to Caribbean golden passports as a backdoor route to Europe now face uncertainty after the European Union, EU, ordered five Caribbean nations to scrap their citizenship-by-investment, CBI, programmes by 2028. The EU’s warning to Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Saint Lucia threatens one of the most popular escape routes for Nigerians frustrated by high Schengen visa refusal rates, delays and non-refundable losses. With Nigeria recording a 47.8 percent Schengen visa rejection rate and applicants losing an estimated €4.5 million in non-refundable fees in 2025 alone, many had opted to pay a minimum of $235,000 for Caribbean citizenship that guarantees visa-free access to most of the EU member states and over 100 destinations globally. Citizenship-by-investment programmes explained Citizenship-by-investment (CBI), a legal process where an individual obtains a second passport and full citizenship in a country by making a large, government-approved financial contribution to its economy, is a widely exploited route by wealthy Nigerians, who seek to hedge against visa restrictions, the volatility of the naira, high Schengen visa rejection rate and the uncertainty of doing global business on a low-ranking Nigerian passport. It allows applicants to include spouses, dependent children under 31, parents and grandparents 55 and over, and unmarried siblings after they have been granted citizenship. An Antigua and Barbuda passport, for instance, offers visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to over 150 destinations, including Hong Kong, Singapore, the UK and Schengen area for minimum non-refundable fees of $230,000. Dominica, on the other hand, starts from $200,000, St Kitts and Nevis $250,000, while Grenada is priced because it holds an E-2 Investor Treaty Visa with the US, allowing citizens to be eligible to apply for a non-immigrant visa. The St. Lucia CBI programme offers a real estate development option and access to over 140 destinations with no prior visa needed. Nigeria among top source countries for CBI Meanwhile, data obtained by Vanguard shows that Nigeria as one of the biggest markets for Caribbean CBI programmes with Nigerian nationals accounting for about 16 percent of applications to Grenada’s programme in Q4 2025, ahead of China at 12 percent, and remained a leading source market in Q1 2026, according to Investment Migration International, IMI Daily, report. Other top applicants were Iraq, USA, Pakistan, Egypt, India, Lebanon, Vietnam and Turkey. Other African countries with high uptake include Egypt, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Angola, Algeria and Morocco. For Antigua and Barbuda, Nigeria ranked third in the top source countries for CBI behind China and US. Annual statistics published by Saint Lucia’s government showed Asia (led by China) as its largest block, with the United States leading the Americas cohort and Nigeria topping the African chart. The EU has now set September 2026 for enhanced screening, a 24-month wind-down, and final deadline of June 1, 2028 to end the programmes entirely. Why Brussels is cracking down The EU has in recent years increased pressure on member states running CBI/RBI schemes, citing security and integrity concerns. Several Caribbean and European programmes have already been suspended or tightened, with more expected to follow. A 2025 EU report flagged the five Eastern Caribbean states for high volumes, short processing times and low rejection rates. Brussels said the programmes allow third-country nationals to bypass visa checks and enter Europe through a “back door.” Past recipients included Mutassim Gaddafi, son of late Libyan leader, Muammar Gaddafi. But the crackdown is global. A joint Financial Action Task Force, FATF, and OECD report warned that properly managed, CBI/RBI programmes can benefit host countries, but in practice bring “significant risks of money laundering, fraud and other forms of misuse.” “Criminal exploitation of citizenship and residency programmes is a multi-billion-dollar business to launder proceeds of fraud and corruption, evade justice, or access third countries,” OECD Secretary-General, Mathias Cormann, said. Criminals, the report said, use new passports to hide identity, open shell companies and move illicit goods, including wildlife products. Given the pressure, the Caribbean itself is reforming. In a landmark move, the five states established the Eastern Caribbean Citizenship-by-Investment Regulatory Authority, ECCIRA, in 2025 to coordinate standards, tighten due diligence and raise prices from sub-$100,000 era to $200,000 in 2024 and $235,000 – $250,000 floor by 2027. St Kitts & Nevis, the oldest programme since 1984, has revoked 13 citizenships for underpayment. In Europe, Malta ended investor citizenship in 2025, Bulgaria and Cyprus shut theirs. Portugal rebranded its Golden Visa as Solidarity Visa, shifting from property to affordable housing and venture capital funds. Greece remains popular. EU, UK others toeing Trump’s stringent immigration stance – Foreign policy Though there’s an ongoing discussion between the EU and the five affected Caribbean nations, foreign policy experts opine that with Brussels threatening to withdraw visa-free access for the five Caribbean countries if they fail to end the schemes, Nigerian applicants may be left stranded. Caribbean leaders met in July 2026 to coordinate a joint response and are expected in Brussels to negotiate. They point to 2024 agreements that raised prices and tightened due diligence. Femi Ojumu, a foreign policy expert and international lawyer, said the planned shut has far-reaching implications, noting that the long-term viability of the CBI schemes are now mired in uncertainty. Ojumu stated that with the aggressive anti-immigration drive of US President Donald Trump, whom he described as the de facto leader of the West, countries like those in the EU, Canada and the UK have followed suit by embedding similar stringent anti-immigration programmes targeting developing countries like Nigeria. He further argued that when this is combined with ever more rigorous anti-money laundering and combating terrorist finance regimes by the USA, EU and other Western countries, the future of the $250,000 global investment initiatives offered by Grenada and other Caribbean nations hangs in the balance. According to him, while these CBI programmes remain critical revenue sources for the Caribbean countries, the tightening global environment “imperils” their viability and “diminishes the attraction of these schemes for Nigerians who invested vast sums, leaving them facing constrained global mobility and heightened risks of sub-optimal return-on-investment.” On the flip side, he said the growing uncertainty may present an opportunity for Nigeria to look inward — to sustainably develop its own economy and socio-political space so that wealthy Nigerians can pragmatically invest at home and in nations with friendlier and more frictionless immigration and trade policies on a win-win basis. Not exit, but sovereign diversity Despite uncertainty, migration consultants said demand from Nigerian entrepreneurs remains strong, though motive is shifting. According to them, Nigerians are no longer buying a passport to leave Nigeria, they are buying a second base to complement Nigeria. Chee Okebalama, Managing Director, Client Advisory at Multipolitan, a leading migration advisory firm, noted that Nigeria has remained “a market of considerable scale” despite the threat of shut down. “Many of our clients in Nigeria are entrepreneurs, and Nigeria remains a market of considerable scale, ambition and commercial opportunity. “That is why CBI and RBI remain compelling. RBI allows families to add a European base in markets such as Greece or Malta while retaining strong economic, personal and commercial ties to Nigeria.” “The objective is not to move away from Nigeria, but to complement it with greater mobility, jurisdictional resilience and long-term choice for family,” she stated. She explained that globally, clients were building “sovereign diversity”, reducing dependence on any one country to hedge policy changes, currency volatility and geopolitical risks. For many, a European residence permit offers a foothold without abandoning operations, staff and investments in Nigeria. Beyond travel, drivers now include education, healthcare, banking options and ability to respond quickly to global opportunities. “Globally, we are seeing the same shift. Our clients are increasingly building multi-jurisdictional lives through alternative residence and citizenship, not simply for visa-free access, but to create sovereign diversity: reducing dependence on any one country and expanding the freedom to live, invest and respond across jurisdictions,” Okebalama explained. What next for Nigerians? Analysts stressed that if Schengen visa-free is withdrawn, the main attraction for African investors disappears and demand from Nigeria could fall sharply. For now, nationals of Mauritius and Seychelles who already enjoy visa-free Schengen access are unaffected. But for Nigerians, with visa rejection rates near 50 percent, closure of the Caribbean route leaves a major gap, forcing a pivot to residency programmes in Greece, Malta, Portugal and Dubai, where physical presence is required but offers longer-term stability. “As per my observation, I believe emerging residence-by-investment options in markets such as Panama, the UAE and Oman will become increasingly attractive in addition to the EU options such as Malta, Portugal and Greece,” she said. According to her, these pathways allow Nigerian entrepreneurs to remain anchored in Nigeria’s entrepreneurial ecosystem while expanding their commercial reach and access to new markets. items.title: First round of talks between govt, opposition end as PTI’s Oct 4 protest looms over Islamabad
items.description: The first round of talks between the PTI-led opposition and the ruling coalition over the party’s proposed Oct 4 long march concluded on Friday, with both sides agreeing to resume the dialogue on Saturday. The meeting between government and opposition representatives, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, was aimed at defusing the country’s ongoing political crisis. It comes ahead of the the PTI’s planned Oct 4 protest march demanding the release of party founder Imran Khan, which has emerged as the latest point of contention between the party and the federal government. According to a statement issued by the NA Secretariat, the participants held detailed discussions “on the prevailing political situation and exchanged views on various matters of national importance”. “The government, PPP and opposition representatives apprised each other of their respective positions and held a detailed exchange of views in a constructive and cordial manner. The participants emphasised the need to resolve national issues through dialogue and negotiations,” it said. The statement added that the second round of talks would be held on Saturday at 2pm in the NA speaker’s chamber. “NA Speaker Sadiq played a key role in facilitating dialogue among the government, PPP and opposition,” the statement said. The delegations were welcomed by Speaker Sadiq upon their arrival. “I am only playing the role of a mediator,” he said. Sadiq said his office was “always open” to resolving issues through negotiations and that he had consistently invited the opposition to engage in dialogue. He maintained that negotiations were the only way to resolve differences and issues, adding that positions and offices were temporary. “Parliament is the only forum where solutions to issues can be found,” he said. In an earlier post on X, the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan said the opposition side was being led by the leader of the opposition in the Senate, Allama Raja Nasir Abbas. Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry attended the meeting, along with PPP Senator Sherry Rehman and National Assembly members Syed Naveed Qamar and Ejaz Hussain Jakhrani. The opposition was represented by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan, Abbas, Amir Dogar, former NA speaker Asad Qaiser and PTI General Secretary Salman Akram Raja. As the PTI remains resolute to go ahead with the march, federal ministers have warned that the Centre would have no other option but to impose governor’s rule or emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in light of the security situation in the province and the PTI’s protest call. For its part, the opposition party has warned the government of dire consequences if such a decision is imposed. ‘PTI will have to call off its march’ Speaking to the media after the meeting, PPP’s Rehman said the party believed in resolving issues through negotiations. She said that PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had stated the party’s stance on the long march and that the PTI had to call it off “unconditionally”. “They will have to call it off rather than postponing or deferring,” she said. “Both parties have time; we will meet tomorrow. We will try to conclude this by tomorrow,” she stated. Talking about the opposition’s reported demand of facilitating a meeting with incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, she said she could not answer the question. However, she said the opposition had asked for time and “we should respect it”. “A political and democratic attitude requires sitting at the negotiation table and resolving the issues through dialogue,” she stated. Later, Bilawal welcomed the government’s decision to work with his party and jointly engage with the opposition “to find political solutions to political problems”. “The challenge of terrorism has become an existential threat to Pakistan, particularly given the active support these groups receive from neighbouring countries,” he wrote on X. The PPP chief expressed hope that the talks would conclude with the opposition unconditionally calling off the long march, which would allow the country to come together to address the threat of terrorism and those from neighbouring countries. “The PPP has been, and will always remain, committed to combating terrorism through any and all constitutional means,” he added. ‘Govt should engage with integrity’ The Senate opposition leader, speaking to the media at his office during a break in talks with the government, said the government should engage with the opposition “with integrity” and take steps towards resolving the issues. “If the government cares about the political crisis, then it should sit with the opposition with integrity and step forward to find a solution,” Abbas said. Regarding PTI’s long march, he said the call would remain “intact” until a solution was found. “Negotiating is the way of political leaders; negotiations could resolve gigantic issues and war,” he said, adding that “it, however, depends on the government’s intention”. He questioned whether the government, as the other party to the negotiations, genuinely wanted to resolve the issues. “They are in government and it is their responsibility to maintain peace, resolve crises, and ensure economic stability,” he said. Abbas reiterated that the outcome depended on how “autonomous” the government was and whether it had the “intent” to pursue negotiations. Speaking to the media after the talks, PTI Chairman Gohar said that both parties had shared their stances on “all the issues”. Regarding negotiations with the government, he added that “Abbas and Mehmood Khan Achakzai have the mandate for these things”. During an opposition alliance meeting yesterday, he said, the party had decided to attend the talks with the government and give their stance if it called on the opposition. “The positive aspect of this talk is that it is still continuing and we’ll meet again tomorrow,” he said, adding that tomorrow’s talks would be held by the same opposition committee that held them today. Asked what the party would do if the PTI were to gain access to Imran and he were to once again call for a long march, he said: “We always act upon the directions given by Khan sahab .” A day earlier, it emerged that a joint delegation of the PPP and the government would hold a meeting with the PTI leadership on Friday, during which the “current political situation” in the country would be discussed with the opposition. The decision came after a meeting at President House attended by President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and other party leaders. Sanaullah also said on Thursday that the federal government and PTI were engaged in “off-the-record talks” regarding PTI’s planned protest. Sanaullah said that the decision on the proposed march rested with PTI’s senior leadership, “with whom off-the-record consultation is ongoing”. “So let us see, even if they do not postpone it, we have arrangements in place to stop them,” he warned.

items.title: Une campagne de sensibilisation et de consultations foraines en santé mentale à Danyi
items.description: Apéyémé, 2 oct. (ATOP) – Une campagne de sensibilisation et de consultations foraines gratuites en santé mentale s’est tenue le jeudi 1 er octobre au centre hospitalier préfectoral de Danyi. L’activité a permis de consulter et de prendre en charge 152 personnes souffrant des crises de perte de connaissance, d’épilepsie, de folie, de colère ainsi que des troubles mentaux du comportement. Les équipes médicales ont également diagnostiqué d’autres pathologies telles que les états dépressifs et les conduites additives liées à l’usage des substances psychoactives. Cette action humanitaire est portée par l’Association santé mentale développement Togo (ASMDT) en collaboration avec la Société togolaise de santé mentale (SoToSaM). Elle a reçu l’appui de l’Expertise France à travers le projet tripartite CHU Campus Lomé, centre hospitalier de Vinatier de Lyon et centre hospitalier Esquirol de Limoge. Le but est d’amener les soins de qualité en santé mentale vers la communauté aussi bien dans la prévention que dans le curatif. L’initiative a permis de sensibiliser la population sur les facteurs de risques des maladies mentales et d’encourager cette dernière à l’acceptation des personnes vivant avec un handicap mental sans discrimination, ni stigmatisation. Le président de l’association des psychiatres du Togo, Prof Wenkourama Daméga a rappelé que la maladie mentale, les troubles mentaux et les problèmes liés à l’usage des substances psychoactives (alcool et drogue) peuvent avoir de graves répercussions sur la santé et la vie des personnes touchées et de leurs proches. Il a conseillé la population à adopter des comportements sains pour éviter ou diminuer les maladies mentales. Pour le préfet de Danyi, Koumagnanou Amavi, cette œuvre humanitaire vient à point nommé soulager les souffrances des malades mentaux et leurs familles. Il a exhorté d’autres bonnes volontés à emboîter le pas aux partenaires pour le bien-être de la communauté. Une unité de soins spécialisés en santé mentale a été mise sur pied dans le district sanitaire de Danyi pour assurer la continuité des soins. ATOP/SKD/DHK

items.title: Ban on durbar, horse riding in Kano remains – Police
items.description: The police command in Kano State has reiterated the ban on Durbar and horse/animal-riding activities across the state, warning violators of the possibility of arrest and prosecution. The Commissioner of Police in the state, Ibrahim Adamu-Bakori, gave the warning at a news conference on Friday in Kano. Aminu-Bakori said the ban, imposed by the Kano State Government after consultations with relevant security stakeholders, remained in force and was binding on everyone irrespective of status or position. He said reports of apparent breaches of the directive had prompted the police and other security agencies to restate the need for strict compliance. “The threats which the ban was put in place to check are still potent,” he said. The commissioner said the primary responsibility of security agencies was to maintain public peace, safety and order, adding that no act capable of jeopardising public safety would be tolerated. He said any individual, institution or organisation intending to organise any form of durbar or horse-riding activities in public places must submit a written request at least 72 hours before the event. According to him, the notice must be submitted to the Office of the Commissioner of Police to enable security agencies to conduct the necessary security assessment and make adequate arrangements for public safety. Aminu-Bakori urged residents to comply with all lawful security directives and cooperate with security agencies to maintain peace and order in the state. He warned that anyone who violated the directive would be arrested and prosecuted, irrespective of the person’s position or status. He assured residents that the police and other law enforcement agencies remained committed to safeguarding lives and property and maintaining peace and order across the state. (NAN) The post Ban on durbar, horse riding in Kano remains – Police appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Finance Minister demands greater returns from NLA after GH¢10 million dividend presentation
items.description: Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson has said the National Lottery Authority (NLA) must generate more revenue for the state, describing its GH¢10 million dividend as a positive step. Receiving the dividend from the NLA’s Board of Directors, led by Board Chairman Frederick Amissah and Director-General Mohammed Abdul-Salam, Dr. Forson said the payment marked the resumption of dividend contributions to the Ministry of Finance after several years. He noted that the NLA had previously paid dividends annually, but the payments stopped after 2017. “The taxpayer deserves more than GH¢10 million from NLA, but this is a good step,” he said. Dr. Forson disclosed that the Ministry was working with the NLA and the Attorney-General to review agreements that had limited the Authority’s returns to the government. He said the review would be completed this month. According to him, some of the agreements had ceded an unreasonable share of the Authority’s revenue to other entities, depriving the state of funds that should have accrued to it. The Minister also urged the NLA to focus on its core mandate and avoid activities outside its statutory responsibilities. “Let this not be symbolic. Ghana deserves better,” Dr. Forson said, pledging to ensure that the state received its due from the Authority. Board Chairman Frederick Amissah said the dividend payment marked the beginning of reforms and improvements at the NLA, assuring the government that the Authority would work to deliver stronger returns in the years ahead. “This is just the beginning of the reforms and improvements in NLA,” he said.

items.title: 2027: Results transmission, violence, intimidation, security collusion top risks, say stakeholders
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Stakeholders in the electoral process have named results transmission and collation, and electoral violence, voter intimidation and security collusion, as the biggest threats to the credibility of the 2027 general elections. They expressed their fears at the first Multi-stakeholder Roundtable on Electoral Reform Implementation, Electoral Integrity and Youth Participation, held in Abuja. The roundtable was convened by Kimpact Development Initiative KDI and other partners on the Youth Electoral Reform Project YERP-Naija. A communique issued at the end was signed by Oluwafemi John Adebayo, Head, Research & Programs, Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI), National & North Central Partner, YERP-Naija; Joan M. Ayala, a Director at the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC); Prince Chinedu Obi of the Inter-Party Advisory Council IPAC; Peters Maduomba, Executive Director, CLEEN Foundation; and Adubaum Michael of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission EFCC. Others who signed are Ziguda Amuba, Executive Director, Jesz Development Foundation; Charles Pius, Senior Anchor/Reporter, News Central TV; Ibrahim Faruk, Program Coordinator, YIAGA Africa; Prof. Julius Bolade Akinson of Bunta Open University; and Abiodun Olagunji-Ali, Deputy Director, National Orientation Agency NOA. In a live audience poll, 58 per cent of participants said the greatest gap between legal provisions and practical implementation lay in “results transmission and collation”. Election Day operations followed with 26 per cent, and pre-election activities such as voter registration, campaigns and logistics scored 16 per cent. On the biggest concern ahead of 2027, 48 per cent picked “electoral violence, voter intimidation and security collusion”. Vote-buying and voter inducement polled 34 per cent, while failures or delays in real-time result uploads through the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) polled 17 per cent. The communique said: “These findings underscore continuing concerns about electoral security, electoral integrity, and public confidence in election administration and results management.” It traced the trust deficit to the 2023 presidential election. “Public mistrust following the 2023 presidential election stemmed primarily from INEC’s failure to timeously upload polling unit results to the INEC Results Viewing IREV portal in line with its guidelines and public commitments,” it said. Participants said the problem persisted in this year’s off-cycle polls. “Delays in uploading results to the INEC Result Viewing IReV portal, including a reported delay of about two hours in Osun, weaken public confidence even where the underlying results are accurate,” the communique stated. It also pointed to gaps in the rules governing the new technology, stating; “The practical weight of the reform now rests on administrative instruments as much as on the Act. The Act gave legal recognition to technology, but it was the INEC guidelines that introduced the electronic copy of the EC8A (e-EC8A). The guidelines leave open questions, such as where discrepancies between the electronic and physical result sheets are reconciled,” it said. On the mood of the electorate, the communique observed that many Nigerians, “particularly young citizens, remain skeptical about the credibility of the electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections.” It added that “vote buying and electoral violence remain a major threat to the credibility of the 2027 general elections.” Among its resolutions, the roundtable urged INEC to make the result management process “more transparent, effective and timeous in line with Electoral Act 2026 and its guidelines”, especially the mandatory transmission of results to the portal. It asked the Police, the EFCC and the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission ICPC to “diligently prosecute vote buyers and sellers, electoral violence perpetrators and other electoral offenders and provide regular statistics on ongoing cases to serve as deterrent for the 2027 elections.” Security agencies were also urged “to maintain strict neutrality, professionalism, and collaboration with stakeholders to secure polling environments and border towns against voter suppression and intimidation.” The communique asked the National and State Assemblies to “expedite legislative measures to establish an Independent Electoral Offences Commission to ensure transparent, prompt, and uncompromised prosecution of electoral offenders as a deterrent.” It called on INEC and other agencies to “scale up early, aggressive public education campaigns well ahead of the 2027 general elections”, covering voter responsibilities and collection procedures for Permanent Voter Cards PVCs. On the leadership of the electoral body, participants asked the National and State Assemblies to amend the constitutional and legislative framework by “establishing an independent, non-partisan, stakeholder-based appointing committee to insulate the electoral umpire from political bias and build public confidence.” The post 2027: Results transmission, violence, intimidation, security collusion top risks, say stakeholders appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Son of ex-Chelsea player dies after fatal UAE desert hike
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The son of former Chelsea player Eddie Newton has died during a desert hike in the United Arab Emirates after his wife had urged him not to go, an inquest has heard. As reported by BBC News on Friday, Cassius Newton, 34, was found dead in the mountainous Wadi Naqab region of the UAE on July 18, hours after he last spoke to his wife. His friend, Aran Martinson, also died during the hike after the pair set off at about 07:00 local time. Newton had called his wife at about 02:00 to tell her about their planned hike, but she asked him not to go because of the expected heat. Area coroner Michelle Brown told Essex Coroner’s Court that temperatures in the area could reach about 40C and feel even hotter inside the canyons. Newton had also been out the previous night, while his wife was concerned that he had not had enough sleep or charged his phone sufficiently. The wives of both men eventually contacted authorities after they failed to hear from them for several hours, prompting a rescue operation. The pair were found between 3km and 4km from where they had parked, with their bodies about 350 metres apart. Both men were taken to hospital in Ras Al Khaimah but were pronounced dead later that day. Brown ruled that their deaths were the result of misadventure, describing the incident as “an intentional trip with unintended consequences”. She said both men died after their body temperatures rose severely, leading to organ failure. The court heard that the route was a recreational hike on a designated trail and normally took about four hours to complete. Newton, originally from Poole, and Martinson had both recently moved to Ras Al Khaimah, where they met through their work at a global company. Eddie Newton, who played for Chelsea before going on to have two spells as the club’s assistant manager, travelled to the UAE to identify his son’s body. Chelsea had earlier expressed its devastation over Cassius Newton’s death. He had also previously been part of the club’s academy. Messages between Martinson and his wife were also read during the inquest. At 09:26, she wrote: “You must be cooking.” After several more hours without hearing from him, she sent another message expressing her distress. Martin­son’s wife later paid tribute to him online, describing him as “incredibly driven, hardworking and ambitious”. items.title: Sánchez, a los grupos que han tumbado los decretos: “Las historia les juzgará antes de lo que creen y con más contundencia de la que imaginan”
items.description: Pedro Sánchez tomó de forma inesperada la palabra al final del debate que se llevó a cabo la mañana de este viernes en el Congreso de los Diputados. Los socialistas, encabezados por la ministra de Vivienda, Isabel Rodríguez, durante la apertura de la sesión habían intentado convencer a la oposición, y especialmente a Junts, de que apoyara o, al menos, se abtuviera en la votación de los dos reales decretos de vivienda, que finalmente han caído con la negativa de las derechas. Aunque no estaba previsto, el presidente del Gobierno subió al estrado escasos minutos antes de la votación para volver a recordar el alcance de los decretos que, aunque imperfectos, resolverían la situación habitacional de cientos de miles de ciudadanos. “Es evidente que sus medidas no van a resolver por sí solas todos los problemas de la vivienda, no lo van a hacer, pero es innegable que sí ayudarán a mitigarlos”, reconoció, e hizo una advertencia a los diputados de que “esta vez la culpa no la tendrá la troika, ni los bancos, la tendrán aquellos que voten no desde su escaño”. Sin embargo nada impidió que los independentistas catalanes se cuadraran en el no, mucho menos tras la sentencia que les lanzó Sánchez: “Las historia les juzgará antes de lo que creen y con más contundencia de la que imaginan”. items.title: Pétrole : les cours reculent, le marché anticipe un déblocage des réserves européennes de gazole
items.description: Les cours du pétrole reculent vendredi, le marché anticipant un déblocage des réserves européennes de gazole sous la pression des Etats-Unis, alors qu'une visioconférence du G7 est organisée dans l'après-midi pour tenter de répondre à la flambée des prix des carburants. Vers 13H55 GMT (15H55 à Paris), le prix du baril de Brent de la mer du Nord, pour livraison en décembre, perdait 1,98% à 100,28 dollars. Son équivalent américain, le West Texas Intermediate, pour livraison en novembre, tombait de 2,93% à 90,15 dollars, après avoir chuté de plus de 5% à 88,06 dollars. Pour soulager le marché mondial, le gouvernement américain presse l'Europe de puiser dans ses stocks d'urgence de gazole, et menacerait même d'interdire ses exportations de carburants vers l'UE en cas de refus. L'échéance des élections législatives de mi-mandat début novembre accroît la pression sur l'administration Trump pour faire baisser les prix de ce carburant très utilisé dans le secteur agricole et le transport par camions de marchandises. Une interdiction des exportations par Washington pourrait en effet réduire les prix domestiques mais elle ferait bondir les cours du gazole pour les pays importateurs, et risquerait d'avoir des répercussions négatives sur d'autres produits raffinés aux Etats-Unis en quelques semaines. Pour la Maison Blanche, l'alternative est que les pays de l'UE puisent dans leurs réserves de gazole pour soutenir le marché. La guerre au Moyen-Orient a fait monter les prix du pétrole brut cette année, mais c'est surtout le marché des produits raffinés qui inquiète avant l'hiver. « La baisse des capacités de raffinage et de la production au Moyen-Orient et en Russie, combinée à l'annulation par la Chine de cargaisons de produits destinés à l'exportation afin de soutenir son approvisionnement intérieur, continue de restreindre la disponibilité des carburants », explique Ole Hansen, analyste chez Saxo Bank. « Un prélèvement sur les réserves stratégiques contribuerait à compenser la baisse des stocks commerciaux » et soulagerait les prix, ajoute à l'AFP Giovanni Staunovo. Cependant, « les réserves stratégiques sont conçues pour faire face à des perturbations temporaires de l'offre, et non à des déséquilibres structurels du marché », rappelle-t-il. Des réserves plus faibles impliquent que « le marché pourrait devenir de plus en plus sensible aux risques pesant sur l'offre, ce qui pourrait se traduire par des fluctuations plus importantes des prix », précise l'analyste. The post Pétrole : les cours reculent, le marché anticipe un déblocage des réserves européennes de gazole appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Democracy has fared well since 1999 — Sokoto Commissioner
items.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — Sokoto State Commissioner for Local Governments and Chieftaincy Affairs, Alhaji Ibrahim Dadi Adare, has said Nigeria’s democratic journey since the return to civilian rule in 1999 has demonstrated the resilience of the country’s democratic institutions despite years of military intervention in governance. Adare, the Dallatun Gobir, stated this in Sokoto while speaking with journalists as part of activities marking Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary. He described the anniversary as an opportunity for Nigerians to reflect on the country’s journey, sacrifices, achievements and challenges since independence. “I want to use this opportunity to celebrate with all Nigerians for witnessing the 66th year of Nigeria’s independence. It is, of course, something to rejoice about and to be happy with,” he said. The commissioner paid tribute to Nigeria’s founding nationalists, including the country’s first Prime Minister, Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa; Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe; Chief Obafemi Awolowo; and Sir Ahmadu Bello, the Sardauna of Sokoto. He said their sacrifices, patriotism and commitment to nation-building laid the foundation for subsequent generations, adding that their emphasis on national unity remained relevant to the country’s contemporary challenges. Adare also acknowledged the contributions of successive military administrations to national development and unity but argued that democratic governance provides citizens with greater opportunities for representation and participation. “Democracy remains the best form of government that is acceptable to all. It is the government of the people, for the people and by the people,” he said. He added, “When compared with democracy, military administration cannot be compared with it. There is always representation at various levels of governance, and people always want to feel a sense of belonging, particularly when it comes to issues of democracy.” Nigeria returned to civilian rule in 1999 after decades of military intervention and has since maintained uninterrupted constitutional civilian rule. Adare said the period had recorded developments in political representation and institutional continuity, while acknowledging the roles of former Presidents Olusegun Obasanjo, the late Umaru Musa Yar’Adua and Goodluck Jonathan in the country’s democratic transition and consolidation. He urged Nigerians to protect democratic institutions through active participation, respect for the rule of law and commitment to peaceful political processes. 2027 elections Adare also urged Nigerians, particularly residents of Sokoto State, to approach the 2027 general elections with commitment to peace, unity and democratic values. “I appeal to Nigerians, particularly the people of Sokoto State, to remain peaceful, united and law-abiding. They should participate actively in the electoral process, obtain their Permanent Voter Cards and vote for credible leaders who will sustain development, peace and good governance,” he said. He appealed to political parties and their supporters to conduct their activities with tolerance and respect for democratic rules, warning against inflammatory rhetoric, violence and intimidation. “Politicians should play politics with decorum, tolerance and respect for democratic rules. They should shun acts capable of causing disunity or violence,” Adare said. Sokoto development On developments in Sokoto State, the commissioner commended Governor Ahmed Aliyu for what he described as interventions under the administration’s nine-point Smart Agenda. He said the agenda had focused on security, education, healthcare, water supply, infrastructure, agriculture, religious affairs, local government administration and economic empowerment. Adare also acknowledged the role of APC leader in Sokoto State, Senator Aliyu Magatakarda Wamakko, whom he credited with providing political guidance, mentorship and support to the administration. He called on citizens to use the 66th Independence Anniversary to renew their commitment to national unity, democratic stability and the collective responsibility of building a more prosperous Nigeria. The National Customers’ Choice Awards Ghana is designed around the customer’s experience as a brand, identify and celebrate businesses that have earned the trust and confidence of their customers through exceptional products, quality service delivery, strong value propositions, and consistent commitment to customer satisfaction. items.title: ICEE Conference: Ghana must get governance right to solve transport problems – Ing. Ludwig Hesse
items.description: Ghana must improve how cities are governed and managed to address its transport problems, Ing. Ludwig Annang Hesse, president of the Ghana Institution of Engineering (GhIE), has said. He said the division of major metropolitan areas among several municipal assemblies made it difficult to plan and manage transport systems that crossed municipal boundaries. “If we don’t get the governance right, if we don’t get the city management right, all the things I’ve done as an engineer, we’ve done big studies, we’ve done big projects, I’ve led projects to change the way we do business, but that’s not worked because the governance element, which should be the first, has not been done,” he said. Ing. Hesse said public transport planning should be done at the metropolitan level rather than by individual municipalities. “If you are going to do public transport, you cannot do it piece by piece. You have to do it as a whole,” he said. He said the same approach should apply to urban planning, including decisions on the location of industries and other developments. According to Ing. Hesse, Ghana also needed a clear authority with the mandate and resources to implement transport plans. He said several transport plans had been developed over the years, but many of their recommendations had not been implemented because responsibilities were spread across different institutions. He said governance should come first, followed by integrated urban and transport planning, with an authority responsible for implementation and enforcement. Ing. Hesse also called for action on immediate transport problems while authorities worked on long-term plans. “Doing nothing is not an option,” he said, calling for attention to traffic lights, road maintenance and other basic transport infrastructure. He was speaking at the Third International Conference on Energy and Engineering organised by the University of Energy and Natural Resources (UENR) in Sunyani under the theme “Engineering the Future: Energy, Agriculture, and Infrastructure Innovations towards Climate Resilience and Sustainable Development.” The conference brings together researchers, industry practitioners, policymakers, and innovators to discuss energy, agriculture, engineering, infrastructure, and environmental issues. It also seeks to connect research with practical solutions and strengthen collaboration among academia, industry, and government. Associate Professor at the School of the Built Environment, University of Reading, Rory Jones, said Ghana’s energy transition must also take into account people who still lack access to electricity. Prof Jones “There are people currently who do not have access to power. So what do you tell those people about energy transition when they don’t have it?” he asked. He said Ghana needed a clear strategy that considered energy access, its existing resources and its long-term energy needs. Mr Jones also called for closer cooperation between government, industry, and academia to turn research into practical solutions and businesses. He said industry could bring its challenges to universities, where researchers could develop solutions that could be turned into businesses. Chief Executive of the Ghana Chamber of Mines, Ing. Dr Kenneth Ashigbey, said Ghana should use the needs of the mining industry to develop local businesses that supply goods and services to mining companies. Chief Executive of the Ghana Chamber of Mines, Ing. Dr Kenneth Ashigbey, He cited inputs such as grinding media and activated carbon as areas where local industries could be developed. “How do we then use these needs that have budgets attached to them to start some industries?” he asked. Dr Ashigbey said stronger collaboration between industry and academia could help turn research and innovation into businesses and create opportunities for local industries.

items.title: RDC : l’épidémie d’Ebola franchit le seuil des 4 000 morts
items.description: L'epidemie d'Ebola en Republique democratique du Congo a franchi le seuil des 4 000 morts. Dans son bilan du 1er octobre, l'Institut national de sante publique (INSP) fait etat de 4 018 deces parmi 8 300 cas confirmes dans les sept provinces actuellement touchees : l'Ituri, le Nord-Kivu, le Sud-Kivu, le Bas-Uele, le Haut-Uele, la Tshopo et le Sud-Ubangi. Le taux de letalite atteint desormais 48,4 %, soit pres d'un deces pour deux cas confirmes. Selon l'INSP, 2 162 personnes ont gueri tandis que 842 patients sont actuellement hospitalises ou places en isolement. Le taux de suivi des personnes ayant ete en contact avec des malades s'etablit a 80,6 %. L'institut souligne toutefois que ces donnees restent evolutives et peuvent encore etre ajustees apres consolidation, validation et harmonisation des informations transmises par les provinces et les equipes chargees de la riposte. L'epidemie, declaree en mai, est desormais la plus meurtriere jamais enregistree en RDC. Elle est provoquee par le virus Ebola Bundibugyo et continue de s'etendre geographiquement malgre un ralentissement de la transmission observe dans certaines zones. Les communautes religieuses mobilisees Le ministere congolais de la Sante a indique le 1er octobre que les communautes religieuses avaient accru leur engagement dans la sensibilisation. Des responsables de differentes confessions se sont reunis au Centre d'accueil Caritas, a Kinshasa, pour examiner les moyens d'ameliorer la diffusion des messages de prevention aupres des fideles. Les discussions ont notamment porte sur la necessite de transmettre des informations fiables, d'encourager les comportements permettant de reduire les risques de contamination et de combattre les rumeurs entourant la maladie. Mgr Donatien Nshole, secretaire general de la Conference episcopale nationale du Congo (CENCO), a insiste sur le role que peuvent jouer les responsables religieux dans la prevention, mais egalement dans la lutte contre la stigmatisation des malades et de leurs familles. Cette mobilisation vise a restaurer la confiance entre les populations et les equipes sanitaires, alors que la desinformation et la mefiance envers les dispositifs de riposte compliquent encore la lutte contre l'epidemie. Sensibilisation et lutte contre les rumeurs Plusieurs initiatives ont parallelement ete lancees pour mieux informer la population sur les modes de transmission du virus et les comportements permettant de reduire le risque de contamination. a Bunia, dans l'est du pays, une campagne de sensibilisation a ainsi cible plus de 2 000 eleves du complexe scolaire Fabia, de la maternelle au secondaire. a Butembo, dans le Nord-Kivu, les personnes âgees ont egalement ete encouragees le 1er octobre a participer a la diffusion des messages de prevention, notamment aupres des plus jeunes. Les medias sont eux aussi mobilises. a Beni, des journalistes ont suivi une formation consacree au fact-checking et a la lutte contre les fausses informations relatives a Ebola. L'objectif est de mieux detecter les rumeurs susceptibles d'alimenter la peur, le refus des soins ou la mefiance envers les equipes sanitaires. 470 millions de dollars d'engagements supplementaires La riposte beneficie egalement de nouveaux engagements financiers internationaux. La presidence americaine du G20 a annonce, le 30 septembre, plus de 470 millions de dollars d'aide supplementaire, portant a plus de deux milliards de dollars le montant total des promesses internationales depuis le debut de l'epidemie. Ces financements doivent notamment soutenir les centres de traitement d'Ebola, les services de sante, les equipes chargees des enterrements dignes et securises, l'acquisition d'equipements de protection ainsi que la surveillance et le suivi des personnes ayant ete en contact avec des malades.

items.title: I never ordered arrest of opposition supporters with Tinubu Must Go T-Shirts – Zulum
items.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has said he has never ordered the arrest of anybody, including a wide talked about members of opposition parties or those criticising his administration. Speaking in Maiduguri on Friday, Zulum said he was shocked when he heard that some people arrested for wearing “Tinubu Must Go” T-shirts by the police in Maiduguri a few days ago were being linked to his government or directive, insisting that he was not aware of the arrest. The governor said, “His attention was focused on restoring peace and rebuilding Borno after years of Boko Haram insurgency, rather than arresting political opponents”. He said he had repeatedly exposed himself to danger to ensure that residents of the state, including members of opposition parties, were protected from Boko Haram attacks and lived in peace. According to Zulum, only “desperate politicians” would order the arrest of opposition supporters, stressing that he was not one of them. The governor also questioned why he would order the arrest of anyone on political grounds, stating that Borno has remained an All Progressives Congress (APC) state for over a decade, with no fear whatsoever of the opposition party winning any elective position. He said, “Borno had remained an APC state since the party came to power in the state for over a decade,” adding that his priority was to restore the state and improve the lives of its people. Zulum said his administration had invested heavily in restoring peace, resettling internally displaced persons, reconstructing communities destroyed by insurgency and establishing schools, hospitals and other public infrastructure. He said the progress recorded in Borno was the result of his administration’s dedication and commitment to rebuilding the state after years of conflict. The governor further said it was common for some people to make what he described as false accusations against political leaders when elections were approaching in an attempt to attract political attention. “Where were they when we were struggling to see that we had restored peace, resettled IDPs, reconstructed destroyed communities and established schools and hospitals?” he asked. Zulum said some of those now criticising his administration had previously praised its efforts but had started portraying the government negatively as the 2027 elections approached. He said his reward for the sacrifices and resources invested in rebuilding Borno was from God, adding that criticism would not deter him from doing more for the state until the end of his tenure. items.title: Mobilisation des investisseurs et partenaires en faveur de la transformation de l’Afrique de l’ouest
items.description: La Banque d’Investissement et de Développement de la CEDEAO (BIDC) a organisé, le 29 septembre 2026 à Lomé, au Togo, le lancement médiatique officiel du Forum d’Investissement de la CEDEAO 2027 (EIF 2027), en prélude au Forum prévu les 7 et 8 avril 2027. L’événement a réuni des représentants de gouvernements, des institutions de financement du développement, des partenaires régionaux, des investisseurs, des dirigeants du secteur privé, des diplomates ainsi que des représentants des médias. Placé sous le thème « Résilience et transformation : naviguer dans un contexte mondial incertain et libérer une croissance inclusive en Afrique de l’Ouest », le lancement a permis de présenter les objectifs et les priorités stratégiques du Forum. Dans son allocution d’ouverture, Dr George Agyekum Donkor, Président de la BIDC et de son Conseil d’Administration, a souligné le rôle essentiel de l’investissement dans la valorisation du potentiel de la région. Il a présenté l’EIF 2027 comme une plateforme destinée à mobiliser des capitaux, renforcer les partenariats et accélérer la transformation structurelle grâce à des investissements durables et inclusifs. S’exprimant au nom du Gouvernement togolais, pays hôte et partenaire officiel de l’événement, Mme Akou Mawussé Adétou Afidenyigba, Directrice de Cabinet, représentant M. Georges Barcola, ministre des Finances et du Budget de la République togolaise, a insisté sur la nécessité de transformer les défis mondiaux en opportunités d’investissement pour la région. Elle a indiqué que le succès de l’EIF 2027 se mesurerait à l’aune des investissements mobilisés, des projets mis en œuvre et des emplois créés. Le lancement a été marqué par une présentation de l’EIF 2027 ainsi que par un panel de haut niveau consacré aux opportunités d’investissement et aux solutions de financement en faveur d’une croissance durable. Des représentants de BARTON HEYMAN LIMITED, de la Chambre de Commerce Africaine et de l’Agence Nationale de Promotion et de Garantie de Financement des PME (ANPGF) du Togo ont notamment mis en lumière les mécanismes de financement innovants et le rôle du secteur privé. Dans son allocution de clôture, M. Ismael Nabé, Ministre du Plan, de la Coopération internationale et du Développement de la République de Guinée et Président en exercice du Conseil des Gouverneurs de la BIDC, a procédé au lancement officiel de l’EIF 2027 et appelé à une collaboration accrue entre les gouvernements, les investisseurs, les partenaires au développement et le secteur privé. Il a mis en avant les ressources de l’Afrique de l’Ouest, son capital humain et son potentiel à s’imposer comme un pôle économique majeur, appelant l’EIF 2027 à servir de catalyseur pour les investissements stratégiques, l’innovation et les partenariats. Ce lancement marque le début des préparatifs de l’EIF 2027, qui réunira promoteurs de projets, investisseurs, institutions de financement du développement, décideurs publics et dirigeants d’entreprises autour des opportunités offertes par des secteurs stratégiques. Le Forum devrait contribuer à accroître les flux d’investissement, favoriser les partenariats public-privé et soutenir le programme de transformation économique de l’Afrique de l’Ouest. **************************** À propos de la BIDC La Banque d'Investissement et de Développement de la CEDEAO (BIDC) est l'Institution de Financement du Développement des quinze États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest. Basée à Lomé, en République togolaise, la Banque s'engage à financer des projets et programmes de développement portant sur diverses initiatives dans les secteurs des infrastructures et des services sociaux de base, du développement rural et de l'environnement, de l'industrie ainsi que des services sociaux, à travers ses guichets dédiés aux secteurs privé et public. Les interventions de la BIDC se font sous forme de prêts à long, moyen et court terme, de prises de participation, d’octroi de lignes de crédit et mise en place d’accords-cadres de refinancement, des opérations d'ingénierie financière et services connexes. www.bidc-ebid.org Contact Presse Unité de Communication et Relations Extérieures asomda@bidc-ebid.org +228 22 21 68 64 L’article Mobilisation des investisseurs et partenaires en faveur de la transformation de l’Afrique de l’ouest est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Luv Fm journalists Clinton Yeboah, Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom selected for UK MEET emerging technology fellowship
items.description: Two journalists with the Kumasi unit of the Multimedia Group, Clinton Yeboah and Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom, have been selected for the UK Media Excellence for Emerging Technology (UK MEET) Fellowship. The two Luv 99.5FM journalists were selected from more than 500 applications submitted by journalists and content creators across Ghana and Nigeria. Their selection places them among the 13 percent of applicants admitted to the fellowship, which seeks to strengthen journalism on science, technology and emerging innovations. The selection process involved independent assessments of eligible applications by two reviewers. Successful candidates were assessed on the strength of their reporting records, clarity of perspective and story pitches built around questions considered worthy of investigation. The fellowship is delivered by Imperial College London through Imperial Global Ghana, with support from the British High Commission. The programme will begin with residential training in Accra, where fellows will engage with researchers working in areas including artificial intelligence, climate change and health technology. Participants will receive practical training in scrutinising scientific and technological claims, verifying information, identifying relevant data and translating complex developments into accessible stories for their audiences. The programme will also feature editorial clinics designed to help fellows refine their story ideas, strengthen their sources and develop publication strategies for their proposed reports. Beyond the training, the fellowship seeks to build professional networks among science and technology journalists across the region, creating opportunities for collaboration and knowledge-sharing. The UK MEET Fellowship comes at a time of growing public interest in emerging technologies and their impact on society. The programme aims to strengthen the role of journalism in ensuring that technological developments are accurately reported, critically examined and presented in ways that the public can understand.

items.title: De l’état d’urgence à la « loi martiale » : comment les cercles MAGA se préparent à contester une défaite lors des midterms
items.description: Dans une interview donnée au magazine Time publiée hier, jeudi 1er octobre, Donald Trump a refusé d’exclure « la possibilité de déclarer l’état d'urgence à l'approche des élections de mi-mandat », qui se tiendront le 3 novembre Full Transcript of Donald Trump’s 2026 Interview With TIME », Time , 1er octobre 2026.'> 1 . Lors de son meeting de campagne hier, dans l'Oklahoma, le président américain a évoqué la possibilité que les Démocrates cherchent à le destituer en cas d’une défaite républicaine Trump Puts on a Midterms Show for an Audience That’s Already Sold », The New York Times , 1er octobre 2026.'> 2 . Aucune loi fédérale ne confère au président de pouvoirs en matière d’élections. L’invocation de l’Insurrection Act pourrait toutefois dissuader les électeurs de se rendre aux urnes. Le texte autorise le président à déployer des troupes pour réprimer une insurrection, une rébellion, des violences intérieures ou tout autre événement qui entraverait l’application de la loi fédérale ou des États en matière de droits civils. Trump a considéré à plusieurs reprises l’invocation de cette loi depuis son premier mandat : en 2020, suite au meurtre de George Floyd par la police de Minneapolis, en juin 2025, réponse aux manifestations anti-ICE dans les rues de Los Angeles, et en janvier 2026, dans le cadre des manifestations à Minneapolis. Selon les derniers sondages, les Républicains devraient perdre le contrôle de la Chambre des représentants suite aux élections, et potentiellement leur majorité au Sénat. Afin de tenter de limiter l’ampleur de la vague bleue qui s’annonce, les Républicains ont engagé à l’échelle des États un redécoupage très controversé des circonscriptions électorales, tandis que des soutiens de Trump dressent des scénarios de prise de contrôle des élections par la Maison-Blanche. À l’été 2025, le spécialiste de la guerre informationnelle Olivier Schmitt avait déclaré, suite au recrutement de Heather Honey par le département de la Sécurité intérieure, qu’il était « impossible que les élections de mi-mandat soient équitables et transparentes ». Honey a joué, aux côtés d’autres activistes MAGA, comme Cleta Mitchell, un rôle central dans l’effort de décrédibilisation des résultats de l’élection présidentielle américaine de 2020, qui a vu la défaite de Donald Trump face à Joe Biden. En dehors de l'administration, d'autres voix poussent en faveur de mesures radicales qui pourraient perturber la tenue du scrutin, comme celle de Steve Bannon, qui avait évoqué l'an dernier un déploiement de la police de l'immigration aux abords des bureaux de vote. Parmi ces voix figure Peter Ticktin, ancien camarade d'école militaire de Trump et l'un de ses principaux avocats dans le procès civil qu'il a intenté contre Hillary Clinton en 2022. En marge d'une conférence organisée début septembre à Las Vegas, Ticktin, resté proche de Trump, a décrit trois scénarios : Le premier, improbable selon lui car les démocrates auraient, sans preuve, déjà triché lors des primaires, serait que les élections de mi-mandat se déroulent sans heurts ; Le deuxième est que Trump prenne des mesures avant le scrutin pour empêcher la fraude ; Le dernier est que Trump déclare la loi martiale autour du 3 novembre, le jour du vote, pour placer les élections sous contrôle fédéral : « Soit la loi martiale, soit il s'efface ». Interrogé sur le risque d'émeutes si Trump tentait de renverser les résultats, Ticktin s'est dit serein : « Croyez-moi, nos forces armées sont bien plus nombreuses qu'eux » The Supporters Urging Trump to Declare Martial Law for the Midterms », The Atlantic , 23 septembre 2026.'> 3 . Selon un responsable de la Maison-Blanche, Ticktin et d'autres conspirationnistes, comme Wayne Allyn Root, qui a appelé Trump en août à déclarer une « urgence de sécurité nationale » en vue du scrutin, ou Tina Peters, qui a obtenu cette année la clémence du gouverneur du Colorado avec l'appui de Trump, ne jouent aucun rôle dans la politique électorale de l'administration. Ils disposent toutefois d'un accès direct au président américain. items.title: VRA warns payment delays, inter-utility debt threaten liquidity despite GH¢8.9bn revenue in 2025
items.description: The Volta River Authority (VRA) has warned that payment delays, inter-utility debt and revenue shortfalls are putting pressure on its liquidity, despite generating GH¢8.9 billion in electricity revenue in 2025. The Chief Executive of the VRA, Ing. Edward Obeng Kenzo, said the financial pressures remain a major challenge to the Authority’s operations and its ability to execute planned projects. He made the remarks during his presentation at the VRA’s annual stakeholder engagement, where he outlined the Authority’s financial and operational performance for the 2025 financial year. According to the VRA’s report, electricity revenue declined by about 4.0%, from GH¢9.291 billion in 2024 to GH¢8.947 billion in 2025. At the same time, the Authority’s cost of sales increased by 4.0%, from GH¢7.479 billion to GH¢7.814 billion. Despite the financial pressures, VRA recorded a net profit of GH¢88 million in 2025, down from GH¢106 million in the previous year. The Authority also recorded a significant improvement in its foreign exchange position, moving from an exchange loss of GH¢695 million in 2024 to an exchange gain of GH¢237 million in 2025. Financial expenses also fell by 24.0%, from GH¢255 million to GH¢194 million, while administrative costs increased by about 14.0 to GH¢1.384 billion. Liquidity Challenge Ing. Obeng Kenzo’s warning comes as VRA continues to face challenges in maintaining sufficient liquidity to support its operations and investment programme. The Authority identified payment delays, inter-utility debt and revenue shortfalls as key factors constraining its liquidity. It also cited difficulties in securing financing for projects, as well as lengthy procurement and approval processes, among the factors affecting project delivery. Generation Performance VRA remained a major contributor to Ghana’s electricity supply in 2025, accounting for 48% of total sector generation. The Authority generated 12,978 GWh, compared with 14,045 GWh generated by Independent Power Producers. Hydropower accounted for 57 percent of the country’s generation mix, while thermal generation contributed 42 percent and solar less than one percent. The Authority is also pursuing additional generation capacity, including the 100MW Anwomaso Phase II, 132MW T3 Repowering Project and 30MWp Akuse Floating Solar Project.

items.title: Sondage CGTN: La « Golden Week » témoigne de la vigueur de l’économie des vacances en Chine
items.description: Pendant les vacances de la Fête nationale, le tourisme réceptif chinois continue de prendre de l'ampleur, avec de plus en plus de visiteurs étrangers venant en Chine pour découvrir son attrait culturel et touristique, son ouverture et son dynamisme. Au cours du premier semestre de cette année, le nombre de ressortissants étrangers entrant en Chine a atteint 22,914 millions, soit une hausse de plus de 20 % par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente. Parmi eux, le nombre d'entrées sans visa a augmenté de 30,6 % par rapport à l'année précédente. Selon une enquête mondiale menée par CGTN, 92,8 % des personnes interrogées ont déclaré que les contenus publiés sur les réseaux sociaux concernant les voyages en Chine ont renforcé leur envie d'en savoir plus sur ce pays et de s'y rendre, tandis que 87 % ont indiqué qu'une visite sur place leur permettrait d'acquérir une compréhension plus complète et plus authentique de la culture, de la société et du développement chinois. L'essor du tourisme réceptif pendant cette période de vacances n'est pas le fruit du hasard. Il reflète les efforts constants de la Chine pour approfondir son ouverture et faciliter les voyages entre le pays et le reste du monde. Ces dernières années, la Chine n'a cessé d'améliorer ses politiques en matière de visas et d'entrée sur son territoire. La politique de transit sans visa de 240 heures s'applique désormais à 57 pays, tandis que 61 pays bénéficient d'une entrée sans visa de 30 jours à Hainan. Les politiques d'exemption de visa unilatérales et réciproques ont encore davantage ouvert les portes de la Chine au monde. Ces mesures ont stimulé les échanges entre les peuples. Au cours du premier semestre de cette année, 17,815 millions de ressortissants étrangers sont entrés en Chine sans visa, ce qui représente 77,7 % de l'ensemble des arrivées étrangères. L'enquête montre que 91,8 % des personnes interrogées ont déclaré que les mesures chinoises de facilitation des visas et de l'entrée sur le territoire ont renforcé leur envie de voyager en Chine, tandis que 89,5 % estiment que la Chine s'ouvre au monde et partage les fruits de son développement. À mesure que les touristes étrangers découvrent par eux-mêmes le train à grande vitesse chinois, les paiements mobiles et les services touristiques intelligents, le « China Travel » est devenu une tendance populaire sur les réseaux sociaux du monde entier, contribuant ainsi à transformer le tourisme de loisirs en une source de croissance durable pour l'économie chinoise. Ce qui incite les touristes étrangers à revenir en Chine, ce ne sont pas seulement les sites historiques et culturels tels que la Grande Muraille et la Cité interdite, mais aussi le confort et l'innovation de la vie moderne. Des paiements mobiles fluides aux trains à grande vitesse en passant par les services de VTC pratiques, ces expériences du quotidien offrent au monde une nouvelle perspective sur la Chine moderne. Il convient notamment de noter que les voyages en Chine axés sur la technologie gagnent également en popularité : certains touristes étrangers dépensent des milliers de dollars pour des itinéraires sur mesure leur permettant de visiter des usines intelligentes de véhicules à énergie nouvelle, de tester la conduite autonome et d'assister à des lancements de fusées. « Visiter la Chine pour découvrir l'avenir » devient une nouvelle tendance. L'enquête montre que 92,2 % des personnes interrogées estiment que les services pratiques tels que les paiements mobiles, le train à grande vitesse et le covoiturage deviennent un élément important de l'expérience de voyage en Chine. Parallèlement, 91,2 % ont déclaré que la Chine offrait un espace permettant la mise en œuvre de nouvelles technologies et de nouveaux produits du monde entier, grâce à la diversité de ses scénarios d'application et à l'importance de son marché de consommation, contribuant ainsi à faire évoluer les industries mondiales vers une plus grande envergure et une meilleure qualité. Le tourisme réceptif constitue une fenêtre importante sur l'économie d'un pays. Derrière les foules qui se pressent aux points d'entrée pendant les vacances se cachent non seulement des flux d'informations et d'argent, mais aussi un flux de confiance. Les touristes étrangers votent avec leurs pieds, manifestant non seulement leur appréciation des paysages et de la culture chinoises, mais aussi leur confiance dans les perspectives économiques du pays. L'enquête a révélé que 89,8 % des personnes interrogées saluent la croissance économique soutenue de la Chine, tandis que 80,6 % estiment que l'économie chinoise peut maintenir sa dynamique positive à long terme, ces deux chiffres restant élevés pour la quatrième année consécutive. Parallèlement, 71,7 % se sont dits disposés à voyager, à visiter ou à étudier en Chine. La hausse continue du tourisme entrant est un signe fort de l'amélioration des perspectives économiques et de la vitalité de la Chine. Comme le dit le proverbe : « Les relations entre États reposent sur les liens entre les peuples, et ces liens se construisent grâce à la compréhension mutuelle. » L'afflux constant de touristes étrangers pendant les vacances reflète non seulement la résilience et la vitalité économiques de la Chine, mais témoigne également de la chaleur des échanges culturels et de l'apprentissage mutuel. La Chine continuera à ouvrir davantage ses portes au monde, tandis que les liens entre les peuples chinois et ceux des autres pays ne cesseront de se resserrer. Alors que la Chine poursuit son développement de haute qualité et ouvre encore davantage son économie, sa croissance soutenue créera davantage d'opportunités pour les pays du monde entier et contribuera à une prospérité partagée. Synthèse de Nadège YAMEOGO Source CGTN Français

items.title: NPP congress: 7,163 delegates to elect national officers in Kumasi tomorrow
items.description: A total of 7,163 delegates from across Ghana are expected to participate in the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) National Delegates Congress and national officers’ elections on Saturday, October 3, 2026, at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi. The congress will be held in two parts, with delegates expected to consider proposed amendments to portions of the party’s constitution before voting to elect national officers. Forty-five aspirants are contesting nine national executive positions, including National Chairman, Vice Chairman, General Secretary, National Organiser, National Women’s Organiser, National Youth Organiser, National Nasara Organiser, National Treasurer and National Communications Director. Proposed constitutional amendments Sources say the proposed constitutional amendments are expected to be fewer than 20. They include proposals that were not implemented during the party’s last constitutional amendment conference in Accra in January 2026, as well as new proposals that the party believes require further consideration. One of the key proposals concerns the designation of the leader of the party. At the January 31 conference, the NPP introduced a provision stating that the National Chairman would be the leader of the party at all material times. However, following further deliberations, the party is proposing an amendment to make the party’s flagbearer the leader of the party. Another proposal concerns the election of Vice Chairpersons. Under the current arrangement, all candidates contest the position of National First Vice Chairman, with the first, second and third Vice Chairpersons determined according to the order of votes received. Under the proposed amendment, candidates would instead apply for and contest specific Vice Chairperson positions. Delegates will also be asked to approve the appointment of three additional Vice Chairpersons who would not be subjected to elections. Other proposals include the creation of Deputy Communications Officer positions and making the IT Officer an executive position. Based on the procedure adopted at the party’s Legon conference, the Chairperson of the Constitutional Amendment Committee or the chairperson’s representative is expected to read out the motions arising from the proposed amendments before delegates vote by voice. Delegate breakdown The election of national executives is expected to be a major component of the congress. The 7,163 delegates are drawn from all 16 regions, with the Ashanti Region recording the highest number at 1,122. Greater Accra follows with 773 delegates, while the Eastern Region has 732. The Savannah Region has the lowest number of delegates at 184, followed by Western North with 223. Of the total delegates, 2,745 are expected to vote in the National Youth Organiser race, while 1,275 will participate in the National Women’s Organiser election and 858 in the National Nasara Organiser contest. The Baba Yara Sports Stadium has been prepared to host the congress, with the city also witnessing increased activity ahead of the event.

items.title: 2 civilians martyred in firing by Indian forces near Kasur border: state media
items.description: State-run Radio Pakistan reported on Friday that two unarmed Pakistani civilians were martyred and another was injured in firing by India’s Border Security Force (BSF) near the border in Kasur. Citing security sources, the report said that three residents of Ladhar village went a few steps ahead of a border pillar when the BSF “opened fire on them without warning”. “The sources said two civilians were martyred while another sustained injuries in the firing. All three individuals were unarmed,” the report said. It identified the deceased as Azmat Rasool and Mohsin Jutt, both residents of Jattan Wali Haveli, Ladhar. “The security sources further said that none of the three individuals had attempted to cross the border fence. They said the incident constitutes a violation of the border agreement and the standard operating procedures governing the Pakistan-India international border,” the report added. “Indian media, while continuing its tradition of a false-flag narrative, labelled the innocent civilians as alleged infiltrators,” the report said. The development comes a day after Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry lampooned India’s claims of “neutralising” a “terrorist” allegedly linked to the Pakistani military, presenting the individual during a press conference. Asked whether the recent allegations could trigger another armed conflict between the neighbours during the press briefing, he affirmed that Pakistan’s armed forces were always ready for any such move and warned of “very harsh” retribution.
